sources.news_title: Rep. Ilhan Omar’s residence searched as part of ongoing criminal investigation, DOJ says - Regional Media News
sources.text:
Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar’s Washington, D.C.-area residence was searched early Monday morning, a Department of Justice spokesperson said, as part of an ongoing criminal investigation.
Sources tell ABC News that the investigation relates to Omar’s immigration paperwork. Omar, who was first elected to the House in 2018, is the first Somali-American in Congress.
In recent history, the Justice Department’s practice has been to advise prosecutors not to take any overt investigative steps against members of Congress or candidates within 60 days of an election. The midterm elections, during which Omar is up for reelection, take place in 22 days, with early voting starting in Minnesota later this week.
Omar came to the U.S. as a refugee when she was a child and has been living in the country since she was 12 years old. She is a U.S. citizen.
“Today in the Washington, D.C. area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice,” a DOJ spokesperson said. “This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation.”
It’s unclear whether Omar was at her D.C.-area residence at the time of Monday’s search. Omar’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the search or her whereabouts.
Omar, who represents Minnesota’s 5th Congressional District, has been a central political target for the administration and its broader efforts to cast the Somali community as criminal and un-American.
“How about Ilhan Omar? She comes from Somalia. She comes from Somalia. They don’t have a government. They don’t have police. They don’t. All they have is crime and squalor. And she comes into our country, and she says, ‘My constitution allows me.’ She’s talking about our constitution, what they’ve done to Minnesota, these people from Somalia, what they’ve done to Minnesota, should never be allowed. And let’s see what happens. JD Vance and our people are looking at it very strongly,” Trump said during a rally on Saturday.
In social media posts earlier this year, Trump also said Omar “should be in jail” and “sent back to Somalia.”
Trump’s remarks directed at Omar have drawn criticism, and Omar said earlier this year that Trump’s rhetoric has led threats against her to “skyrocket.”
The White House referred all comment requests to the Department of Justice.
Vice President JD Vance, who the administration has tasked with leading the so-called “anti-fraud efforts” said during a White House briefing in May that the administration was going to look into Omar for immigration fraud allegations.
Omar has previously denied any wrongdoing and has not been charged with a crime.
Last month, White House border czar Tom Homan confirmed in an interview with Fox News that the Department of Homeland Security was looking into Omar, but wouldn’t disclose the extent of those allegations noting that it was part of an “ongoing criminal investigation.”

sources.news_title: Immigration agents search Congresswoman Ilhan Omar’s home
sources.text:
WASHINGTON - US immigration agents searched the home of Minnesota Representative Ilhan Omar on Monday morning as part of a “criminal investigation”.Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents “executed a judicially authorized search warrant” for the home in the Washington, DC, area, a US justice department spokesperson told the BBC.
The search “is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation,” the spokesperson said, but no further details were given. US Congress is currently out of session and it is unclear if Omar was at the home. Omar, an outspoken critic of President Donald Trump, described the search as “an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement.” “For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns,” Omar said in an online statement. “This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced.”
Her communications director Jacklyn Rogers called the raid “an outrageous abuse of power” by the Trump administration. “The Congresswoman has done nothing wrong.”
The nature of the criminal investigation remains unclear. A BBC crew saw several agents at the home, some carrying boxes to a van. News of the search was first reported by Fox News, which has said the investigation is about immigration paperwork filed by her late father when Omar was a child. The timing of Monday’s raid — 22 days to the November midterm elections which will decide the balance of power in Congress for the next two years — has raised concerns from Democrats who have rallied behind Omar. The justice department has a longstanding policy of refraining from most enforcement action that is “likely to raise an issue or the perception” it was being brought for the purpose of affecting any election or disadvantage a candidate. The US House Democratic Party leadership said in a statment that Omar was targeted with “vile personal attacks and baseless accusations.” “Now, less than 30 days until the midterm election, his violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family.”
Omar’s immigration records have been scrutinised in the past by Republicans. Earlier this year, fellow Congresswoman Nancy Mace of South Carolina unsuccessfully filed a subpoena of her records.
Last month, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told a conservative podcaster “something is going to happen”, making allegations of marital fraud against Omar. Separately, the White House border tsar Tom Homan told Fox News Omar was being investigated for unspecified immigration violations.
Omar, a Democrat, denied these allegations last month. “I will say it again so it’s as clear as possible: I’m not at all worried about these investigations, because they are complete shams,” she said in a campaign fundraising email, an archive of which has been seen by the BBC.
She has been targeted by Trump with the president previously suggesting that she “should go back” to Somalia and that she should be deported. US citizenship is required to serve as a US House Representative.
Omar has responded to Trump’s insults and attacks describing them as an “unhealthy and creepy obsession.”
The president also spoke unfavourably about the Somali American community. Last week, he wrote on social media that Minnesota “is being taken over by Somali immigrants” and said “the people of Minnesota must fight back.”
Republicans celebrated the search. “Nobody is above the law,” said Minnesota Representative Tom Emmer. “We look forward to learning more details about this raid and investigation.
Omar is the first Somali-American elected to the US House of Representatives and she represents a district in the Minneapolis area. She and Michigan Representative Rashida Tlaib were the first Muslim women elected to Congress.
She won the 2024 election with 74% of the vote.
Minnesota Governor Tim Walz also criticised the search on Monday. “Americans see this for what it is - President Trump is abusing his power to go after political opponents weeks before an election.”
Minnesota senator Tina Smith said called it “a transparent attempt to interfere in our elections.”

sources.news_title: DHS searched Ilhan Omar’s home as part of immigration fraud investigation
sources.text:
DHS Searched Ilhan Omar's Home as Part of Immigration Fraud Investigation
Top administration officials have all but pronounced her guilty in an ongoing investigation.
On Monday, CBS News reported that federal agents searched the Washington, D.C., home of U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar (D–Minn.), as part of an ongoing investigation that "centers on Omar's immigration paperwork."
In a statement to the Associated Press, the Justice Department said agents from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI)—an office within the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) that conducts federal criminal investigations into immigration fraud and identity and benefits fraud—"executed a judicially authorized search warrant" as "part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation."
The search warrant reportedly "lists a series of potential immigration crimes under investigation, including false statements and fraud in immigration paperwork, as well as a general conspiracy charge," according to The New York Times. The Times reported that federal officials are also investigating "whether Ms. Omar derived citizenship from a father who may have been ineligible to obtain naturalized status." In a statement, Omar called the investigation an "outrageous abuse of power and an unprecedented escalation in the weaponization of federal law enforcement to target political enemies," stating she did "nothing wrong."
Omar has been in the Justice Department's crosshairs since January, when President Donald Trump announced that the department and Congress were "looking at 'Congresswoman' Illhan Omar, who left Somalia with NOTHING, and is now reportedly worth more than 44 Million Dollars."
Trump was referencing an investigation by the House Ethics Committee, based on a 2025 financial disclosure form showing she and her husband held assets worth between $6 million and $30 million, a notable increase from her previous filings. Omar later filed an amended disclosure form that showed the assets were worth $18,004 to $95,000 after accounting for liabilities. However, in September, the Wall Street Journal reported that the Office of Congressional Conduct—which reviews allegations against House members and their staff—voted 5–1 to recommend that the House Ethics Committee dismiss the allegations. Per the Journal, investigators found no "substantial reason to believe that Rep. Omar reported false or incomplete information in her financial disclosures." Omar's office told the Journal she didn't catch the errors, which stemmed from erroneous valuations of her husband's businesses, because she "isn't involved in her husband's businesses and trusted the accountant involved."
The investigation into Omar appears to be part and parcel of the Trump administration's weaponization of government—which the president vowed to end—adding to a list of cases that includes former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson, former FBI Director James Comey, and former National Security Adviser John Bolton.
Omar's opposition to the Trump administration's immigration enforcement efforts, particularly in her home state of Minnesota, and her Somali heritage have made her a frequent target of the president and his allies.
Last December, a federal indictment revealed a nearly $9 billion fraud scandal in Minnesota, much of it tied to the state's Somali immigrants. In March, Vice President J.D. Vance—who leads the Trump administration's anti-fraud task force—told right-wing commentator Benny Johnson that Omar "definitely committed immigration fraud against the United States of America." Vance accused Omar of "being at the center of a lot of the worst fraudsters in the Somali community."
Vance doubled down in May, telling White House reporters the immigration fraud allegations were "something that the Department of Justice is looking at right now." He appeared to pull back from his March claim that he was certain Omar had committed immigration fraud, instead stating that while he didn't want to "prejudge an investigation," it "certainly seems like something fishy is there."
In September, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin told Johnson that the investigation into Omar was still "ongoing," and that the department knew she had "married her brother to try to bring him into the United States." Omar's office has denied the accusations, which were first levied against her in 2016.
Mullin claims the investigation into Omar is "not political." He could be telling the truth; federal investigators have scrutinized Omar before. In 2024, the Biden administration's Justice Department opened an investigation into Omar's "finances, campaign spending and interactions with a foreign citizen," according to The New York Times. Per the Times, the investigation eventually "stalled for lack of evidence."
But Mullin's words are also hard to take at face value. Despite denying accusations of weaponizing the justice system, the Trump administration has time and again used dubious legal reasoning to investigate the president's political enemies. This includes New York Attorney General Letitia James, who, after successfully suing Trump for financial fraud, was indicted for mortgage fraud by Trump's Justice Department, which used the same petty justification on her.
The president has also continued a campaign to indict Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, announcing last week that the White House would hold in-person hearings to look into claims she committed mortgage fraud. Ousting Cook would ostensibly allow the president to install a Fed governor aligned with his priorities. It's a tactic that failed Trump once before, when his Justice Department opened a criminal investigation into former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell for his handling of renovations at the central bank's headquarters. Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, dropped the probe in April, and the department ultimately found nothing criminal in Powell's conduct.
An investigation will reveal whether Omar broke the law. Still, if it's anything like the Trump administration's previous efforts, the investigation is likely driven by political animus, not criminal behavior.

Democrats & Social Media Condemn Search of Ilhan Omar's Home
Smells Like Weaponization: Rep.Ilhan Omar Home Searched By Federal Agents
Omar stated on her X (formerly Twitter) account, telling followers, "I will not be silenced," and calling the move "political intimidation."
Share the post
Share this link via
Or copy link
- Two people familiar with the matter told the Associated Press that Omar is part of an ongoing criminal investigation.
- Omar stated on her X (formerly Twitter) account, telling followers, "I will not be silenced," and calling the move "political intimidation."
- Congressional Democrats immediately condemned the move.
Donald Trump and his loyal cronies claimed that former President Joe Biden weaponized the government against him, but it would seem the current occupant of the White House is the one doing all the weaponizing.
The Associated Press reported that federal agents searched the home of Democratic U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar, who also just happens to be on Trump and his administration’s favorite targets, and for obvious reasons, being that she is Somali American. The Somalian’s in her home state of Minnesota have been accused of fraud without a shred of proof.
Two people familiar with the matter told the Associated Press that Omar is part of an ongoing criminal investigation.
Per the AP:
The search was conducted by Homeland Security Investigations agents, said the people, who were not authorized to publicly discuss an ongoing investigation and spoke to The Associated Press on the condition of anonymity. More details about the investigation were not immediately clear, though Vice President JD Vance has in the past accused Omar of committing immigration fraud — an allegation she has denied — and has said he and a top White House official were trying to figure out how to investigate the Minnesota congresswoman.
Omar stated on her X (formerly Twitter) account, telling followers, “I will not be silenced,” and calling the move “political intimidation.”
Congressional Democrats Slam The Search of Rep. Ilhan Omar’s Home
Congressional Democrats immediately condemned the move. Michigan Rep. Debbie Dingell called the search of Omar’s home “unprecedented, but unfortunately not surprising,” adding Trump “repeatedly targeted Congresswoman Omar with hateful rhetoric, contributing to death threats and violence.”
Arizona Rep. Adellita Grijalva said it is “the latest — and darkest — chapter of Trump’s racist political persecution against Ilhan Omar and the entire Somali-American community.”
Colorado Rep. Jason Crow said the obvious, but very quiet part out loud, saying the current occupant of the White House is “weaponizing our government against his perceived political opponents,” while pointing to the administration’s unsuccessful attempt to indict him and other Democrats over a video telling soldiers not to follow illegal orders.
Social media agrees with Crow, immediately calling the search of Omar’s home flat-out weaponization.
Welp.

sources.news_title: Homeland Security agents search home of Rep. Omar
sources.text:
Federal agents executed a search warrant at the home of Rep. Ilhan Omar of Minnesota on Monday, according to three people briefed on the matter, the kind of investigative step the Justice Department has long shied away from so close to an election.
The court-approved search of her Washington-area home comes after Department of Homeland Security officials said in recent months that they were investigating Omar, a Democrat, over her family’s immigration paperwork. More recently, some federal investigators have also sought to investigate other issues, such as Omar’s finances, campaign funds and interactions with a foreign citizen, as The New York Times previously reported.

sources.news_title: Federal immigration agents raid home of Congresswoman Ilhan Omar
sources.text:
In the United States, federal immigration agents have carried out an early morning raid at the home of a high-profile Democratic congresswoman.
Investigators from the Department of Homeland Security searched the Washington DC address of Ilhan Omar, the Somali-born congresswoman who came to prominence as part of an informal group of leftwing politicians known as ‘the Squad’.
The raid comes less than a month before she faces a battle for re-election.

sources.news_title: Homeland Security raids Rep. Ilhan Omar’s residence
sources.text:
Federal officers raided Minnesota Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home early Monday morning, reportedly related to an investigation into the lawmaker’s immigration paperwork, filed by a relative when Omar was a child.
The search was conducted by Homeland Security Investigations, a branch of the Department of Homeland Security that manages criminal investigations, and, according to a Justice Department spokesperson, “executed a judicially authorized search warrant” the agency secured. An anonymous source reportedly “familiar with the situation” alleged to NBC News that the raid was part of a yearslong investigation involving whistleblowers. CNN also reported that a federal judge approved the search warrant but did not name the judge.
White House border czar Tom Homan, the acting head of ICE, stated on Fox News last month that Homeland Security was investigating Omar for alleged unspecified “criminal” conduct, but claimed he couldn’t “give the specifics of what’s happening.”
“If someone committed an immigration violation, if someone committed marriage fraud or anything like that, regardless if they’re a congressman or not, no one’s above the law,” Homan said at the time. “So, I’ll leave it at that. We’ll let HSI, Homeland Security Investigations, continue the investigation.”
In a Monday morning Fox interview, Homan confirmed that the search had taken place.
Omar immigrated to the US from Somalia in 1995, when she was 12, amid the ongoing civil war in the country. She became a naturalized US citizen in 2000. President Donald Trump and his administration have regularly racially targeted Omar—a progressive Democrat and frequent critic of the administration’s policies—fueling further violent threats against her and other lawmakers of color, and people from Somalia living in Minnesota.
Trump and other White House officials have repeatedly cited the Feeding Our Future fraud scandal that involved members of the state’s Somali American community to justify the mass violence by immigration officers in the area as part of ICE’s Operation Metro Surge in late 2025.
The timing of the raid on Omar’s Washington-area home—22 days before the November midterms, in which she is a heavy favorite for reelection—adds additional scrutiny, as Justice Department policy prohibits federal prosecutors and agents from timing investigations or charges to affect election outcomes. While not a binding rule, the Justice Department has historically complied by pausing all related actions in the 60 days before an election. (Trump and the wider MAGA movement have repeatedly targeted former FBI head James Comey, and that agency as a whole, in part over the timing and supposed political motivations of the FBI’s own investigations under Comey into both Trump and former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton.)
“Americans see this for what it is,” Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz, a Democrat who the Trump administration has also targeted, wrote on social media. “President Trump is abusing his power to go after political opponents weeks before an election.”
“I’m ok. Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement,” Omar posted on social media Monday afternoon. “This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced.”

sources.news_title: Rep. Ilhan Omar's Home Reportedly Raided by DHS Agents as Feds Investigate Alleged Immigration Fraud
sources.text:
Rep. Ilhan Omar’s Home 'Raided by DHS Agents' as Feds Investigate Alleged Immigration Paperwork Fraud
Oct. 12 2026, Published 1:18 p.m. ET
Department of Homeland Security agents reportedly raided the home of United States Representative Ilhan Omar, RadarOnline.com has learned.
The Democratic politician is the target of a federal investigation under the orders of President Donald Trump. However, the scope of the investigation wasn't immediately clear.
Markwayne Mullin Announces Investigation Into Omar
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin confirmed an “ongoing investigation” into Omar and hinted “something’s going to happen.”
Mullin insisted Omar had a hand in fraudulent immigration efforts.
"We know that she married her brother to try to bring him into the United States. We know he lives now in London," he alleged.
He further speculated Omar could be engaged in "illegal activity" if the marriage allegations were true. Mullin confirmed the department could be willing to deport Omar, despite her status as a member of Congress.
"There's no expiration to that. If we can prove it that, maybe you shouldn't have been here in the first place; we'll deport you," Mullin said.
Omar's street was blocked off ahead of the raid with agents near her household. The Justice Department confirmed a search was authorized through a judicial search warrant in the area, but did not specifically name Omar as the target, according to the Associated Press.
“This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation,” the department said in a statement.
Trump Vows DOJ Inquiry Into Omar
Trump hasn't been private about his suspicions of the lawmaker. He confirmed the Justice Department was examining allegations made against Omar, calling for her to "go back" to Somalia, despite being naturalized into the United States at 17 years old.
"Additionally, the DOJ and Congress are looking at 'Congresswoman' Illhan Omar (sic), who left Somalia with NOTHING, and is now reportedly worth more than 44 million dollars. Time will tell all," the president wrote in January 2026 after sending White House Border Czar Tom Homan to Minnesota, the state Omar represents.
At the time, Omar brushed off Trump's threat. Her office claimed she had not yet been issued any formal notice from the DOJ about an investigation.
"Sorry, Trump, your support is collapsing, and you're panicking," she wrote. "Right on cue, you're deflecting from your failures with lies and conspiracy theories about me. Years of 'investigations' have found nothing. Get your goons out of Minnesota."
Omar has denied the allegations.
DHS Declines to Elaborate
The DHS has previously declined to share additional details about the investigation. However, Mullin insisted their work was not "political."
A DHS spokesperson said, "As a matter of policy, DHS does not comment on specific investigative techniques, ongoing investigations, or potential future actions. No one, including members of Congress, are above the law."
Trump Admin on the Case
Trump's administration was confident there was an investigation under way – and they weren't quite as secretive as the DHS.
“It certainly seems like something fishy is there, but everybody’s entitled to equal justice under the laws,” Vice President JD Vance said May. “So we’re going to investigate it. We’re going to take a look at it. If we think there’s a crime, we’re going to prosecute that crime.”

sources.news_title: Federal agents search home of Trump critic Ilhan Omar: government
sources.text:
Federal agents search home of Trump critic Ilhan Omar: government
Washington – US federal agents searched the Washington home of Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar on Monday as part of a criminal investigation, officials said, marking a dramatic escalation in President Donald Trump’s confrontation with the outspoken lawmaker.
The search was conducted by agents from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the investigative arm of US immigration enforcement, according to Fox News, citing sources familiar with the matter.
The operation, just three weeks before Omar seeks re-election in the November 3 midterms, raised concerns about longstanding Justice Department practices intended to prevent law enforcement actions from influencing elections.
The cable network reported that the operation was linked to a criminal fraud investigation concerning immigration paperwork submitted on behalf of the Somali-born congresswoman by her late father when she was a child.
Trump’s border enforcement chief Tom Homan told Fox News he was unwilling to give details ahead of any official announcement but confirmed that an “investigation was ongoing for a while” and that “there was a warrant executed this morning.”
US media quoted the Justice Department confirming that agents had carried out a court-authorized search in the Washington area, but officials did not identify Omar or disclose the nature of the investigation.
The search reportedly began around 6:00 am. Video footage apparently taken by a member of the public and posted to X showed several agents wearing HSI jackets outside Omar’s Washington residence.
Omar, 44, is a leftist Democrat and fierce critic of Trump, particularly his administration’s sweeping crackdown on immigration.
The Republican president has repeatedly clashed with Omar, who came to the United States from Somalia as a child and has frequently been the target of his political attacks.
– Rare offense –
In September, Homan said that Omar was the subject of an ongoing criminal investigation, but again declined to provide details.
Omar said at the time that Homeland Security officials had not contacted her about any investigation, dismissing the allegations against her as politically motivated attacks.
There was no immediate public response from Omar to Monday’s search. AFP has sought comment from her office and the Trump administration.
But Xochitl Hinojosa, a former director of public affairs at the Justice Department, criticized the timing of the search.
“There’s a longstanding rule at DOJ that you don’t take overt actions like this before an election, especially when there’s a candidate on the ballot,” she wrote on X.
Aaron Reichlin-Melnick, a senior fellow at the American Immigration Council, wrote on X that the “precedent set by this action is chilling,” warning that raids targeting political candidates shortly before elections could become more common.
Omar was first elected to Congress in 2018 and represents a district including Minneapolis, home to one of the largest Somali communities in the United States.
She is a member of the group of left-wing Democratic lawmakers known as “The Squad,” who have been among Trump’s most vocal opponents in Congress.
No charges against Omar were announced in connection with Monday’s search.
Trump and his Republican allies have for years argued that non-citizens vote in significant numbers in US elections, a criminal offense punishable by imprisonment and deportation.
But studies consistently find non-citizen voting to be too rare an offense to have affected the outcome of any federal election.
An election fraud database kept by the conservative Heritage Foundation, dating back decades, contains just 1,619 cases of election-related offenses — of which non-citizen voting makes up a tiny 5.5 percent.

sources.news_title: Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington home as part of a criminal investigation
sources.text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Federal agents on Monday searched the home of Democratic U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar, a startling escalation in a criminal investigation that brings renewed scrutiny to the frequent target of Trump administration derision in the final weeks of her reelection bid.
The search of the Minnesota congresswoman’s home so close to next month’s midterm contests that will determine control of the House and the Senate was swiftly condemned by top Democrats in Congress and raised questions about the timing given longstanding Justice Department protocol to avoid overt investigative steps involving political candidates in the direct run-up to an election.
The Justice Department confirmed in a statement that Homeland Security Investigations agents executed a judicially authorized search warrant in the Washington, D.C., area in connection with an ongoing federal criminal investigation but provided no other details.
The nature and scope of the investigation were unclear, though officials in President Donald Trump’s administration have repeatedly hinted at the existence of an inquiry targeting Omar, a Somali-born Democrat whose status as an immigrant to the U.S. and left-wing views have repeatedly drawn criticism from Republicans and senior Trump officials.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said last month that there was an “ongoing investigation” related in part to whether Omar lied on her immigration forms and that “something’s going to happen.”
Though the Republican focus on Omar’s background dates back years, the search of her home took place three weeks before the November midterms, in which Omar is on the ballot for reelection. The Justice Department has historically sought to avoid public investigative actions involving a candidate within 60 days of a primary or general election.
“For years, Donald Trump and far-right extremists have relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Omar with vile personal attacks and baseless accusations,” top House Democratic leaders said in a statement. “Now, less than 30 days until the midterm election, his violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family.
An email seeking comment was sent Monday to a representative for Omar.
Trump has frequently targeted Omar
Trump and fellow Republicans from the highest ranks of party leadership have repeatedly and publicly criticized the Somali-born Omar over her status as an immigrant to the U.S. and her left-wing views. Trump as recently as this past weekend brought up Omar at a rally in Tennessee, where he attacked her upbringing and suggested that Vice President JD Vance “and our people” were investigating her.
Vance has in the past accused Omar of committing immigration fraud — an allegation she has denied — and has said he and a top White House official were trying to figure out how to investigate her.
The Justice Department said in a statement Monday that HSI agents executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the department in the Washington, D.C., area but provided no other details. The street was blocked off Monday morning as HSI agents remained near the home.
“This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation,” the department said.
A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security, of which Homeland Security Investigations is part, referred questions about the search to the Justice Department.
Omar has long been a target for Republicans
Omar, who was first elected to the House in 2018, represents Minnesota’s 5th District, including Minneapolis. She is part of The Squad of progressive lawmakers who are a vibrant political force on the left wing of Congress but have also endured repeated attacks from Trump, dating back to his first term. She was one of the first two Muslim-American women in the House and the first African refugee to be elected to Congress.
When Republicans swept control of the House in 2023, they voted to oust Omar from the House Foreign Affairs Committee, citing her anti-Israel remarks.
In January, Trump lashed out at Omar during a rally in Iowa hours before an assailant sprayed the congresswoman during her own town hall meeting in Minneapolis with a substance that turned out to be vinegar. The attacker was sentenced recently to 14 months in prison.
Republicans have raised questions about Omar’s past since before she was even elected, including asserting that she had married her brother and committed immigration fraud. Omar has broadly denied the allegations as “disgusting lies.”
“It certainly seems like something fishy is there, but everybody’s entitled to equal justice under the laws,” Vance told reporters in May. “So we’re going to investigate it. We’re going to take a look at it. If we think there’s a crime, we’re going to prosecute that crime.”
In a separate interview with conservative podcaster Benny Johnson, Vance said without offering evidence that “we actually think that Ilhan Omar definitely committed immigration fraud against the United States of America.”
He said that he and deputy White House chief of staff Stephen Miller had been discussing it and “trying to look at what the remedies are.”
“That’s the thing that we’re trying to figure out,” he said. “What are the legal remedies now that we know that she’s committed immigration fraud. How do you go after her? How do you investigate her? How do you actually do the thing? How do you build the case necessary to get some, some, some justice for the American people?”
Omar’s office has defended her against past allegations
Omar’s office in March dismissed Vance’s claims as fabricated and defamatory.
“This is rich coming from someone who literally said they were willing to ‘create stories’ to redirect the media,” Omar’s chief of staff, Connor McNutt, said in a statement.
“This is a ridiculous lie and desperate attempt to distract from the pedophile protection party’s unpopular war of choice, increasing gas prices, and rapidly dropping polling numbers,” McNutt said at the time of the vice president’s allegations and comments.
___
Associated Press writers Lisa Mascaro, Michelle L. Price and River Zhang in Washington, Kathy McCormack in Concord, N.H., Mike Catalini in Morrisville, Pa., and Meg Kinnard in Columbia, S.C., contributed.

GOOD MORNING, PORTLAND! First and foremost, happy Indigenous Peoples Day (and may Columbus Day rot in hell). Expect mostly sunny skies this week with crisp temperatures tiptoeing down to the low 40s in the morning, with highs topping out at around 65 today through Wednesday. And now let’s tiptoe into some NEWS! (Careful not to step in anything.)
IN LOCAL NEWS:
• The case of Councilor Dan Ryan’s “disappearing cell phone” gets screwier and screwier! As we reported last week, a court ordered Ryan to refrain from deleting messages off his personal phone and other devices, which may contain public records that aren’t being shared with the public. (BTW, city employees aren’t allowed to conduct business on their personal phones in the first place.) But oopsy! Ryan told the court he was no longer in possession of that phone because his spouse traded it in—on the very same day the judge issued a temporary restraining order. (What a coincidence!) But after the Mercury—who’s suing Ryan to get any missing public records—wrote about the disappearing phone, it suddenly reappeared late last week. (What a coincidence!) Ryan filed an October 8 declaration stating that, actually, the phone had not been traded in, but is still in his possession. This flip-flopping of facts did NOT please Multnomah County Circuit Court Judge David F. Rees, who scolded the councilor, saying, “This is not a game of cat and mouse. There are some indications that those games are being played, and it has to stop today.” (I think the Mercury is the “cat” in this scenario.) sources.news_title: Federal agents raid anti-Israel US congresswoman's home amid reported immigration fra
sources.text:
Federal agents searched the Washington, D.C., home of Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar on Monday as part of a federal criminal investigation reportedly involving immigration fraud allegations, in an extraordinary operation targeting one of President Donald Trump's most prominent political critics just three weeks before the US midterm elections.
The early morning search was carried out by agents from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the investigative arm of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The Justice Department confirmed that agents had executed a search warrant authorized by a judge, but did not publicly specify the nature of the investigation.
The department said the operation was part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation. Fox News reported that investigators were examining immigration documents completed by Omar's late father when she was a child. 
The search has attracted significant attention because Omar, a progressive Democrat representing Minnesota, has long been a target of attacks by Trump and other senior Republicans. Its timing, less than a month before congressional elections, has also raised questions about the Justice Department's longstanding practice of exercising particular caution when conducting politically sensitive investigations close to an election.
CNN described the operation as an unusually aggressive investigative step against a politician actively seeking reelection.
Immigration fraud allegations and claims Omar married her brother
Omar, who was born in Somalia, arrived in the United States at age 12 after her family spent time in a refugee camp in Kenya. She was elected to the House of Representatives in 2018, becoming, alongside Palestinian American Democrat Rashida Tlaib, one of the first two Muslim women elected to Congress.
Since then, she has won reelection three times and is now seeking a fifth term representing Minnesota's 5th Congressional District, which includes Minneapolis.
Republican politicians and conservative commentators have for years raised allegations about Omar's immigration history, including an unsubstantiated claim that she married her brother to help him obtain immigration status or student loans.
Omar married British citizen Ahmed Nur Said Elmi in 2009, and the couple divorced in 2017. She has repeatedly denied that Elmi is her brother, describing the allegations as "disgusting lies."
Republicans have also accused her of tax irregularities and suggested that she entered the United States in 1995 using a false name or different family identity to circumvent delays in refugee applications.
Those allegations have not been established as fact, and the Justice Department has not publicly confirmed whether they are directly connected to Monday's search.
Vance accused Omar of immigration fraud without presenting evidence
In May, Vice President JD Vance publicly accused Omar of immigration fraud, saying that he and Deputy White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller were exploring ways to investigate the Minnesota congresswoman.
"It certainly seems like something fishy is there, but everybody's entitled to equal justice under the laws," Vance said at the time.
He said officials intended to examine the allegations and pursue prosecution if investigators found evidence of criminal wrongdoing.
In a separate interview with conservative podcast host Benny Johnson, Vance made a more categorical accusation, claiming without presenting evidence that Omar had committed immigration fraud against the United States.
Omar's office strongly rejected the accusations.
Her chief of staff, Connor McNutt, accused Vance of deliberately spreading falsehoods to distract attention from the administration's policies and political difficulties.
"This is rich coming from someone who literally said they were willing to 'create stories' to redirect the media," McNutt said.
He described the allegations as a ridiculous lie and an attempt to divert attention from the administration's war with Iran, rising gasoline prices and declining Republican polling numbers.
McNutt also used the phrase "pedophile protection party" in his criticism of Republicans, referring to allegations that the Trump administration had sought to prevent the release of documents connected to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
Trump calls for Omar to be institutionalized
Omar has become one of Trump's most frequent targets, particularly over her progressive political positions, criticism of Israel and outspoken opposition to his immigration policies.
Trump and senior administration officials have also repeatedly criticized Minnesota's large Somali American community, of which Omar is a member.
Earlier this year, the administration launched a major immigration enforcement operation in the region involving ICE agents. Omar and her allies accused Trump of employing anti-Somali and anti-Muslim rhetoric, while the congresswoman described the president's repeated focus on her as a disturbing and unhealthy obsession.
The confrontation intensified in February, when Trump said Omar and Tlaib should be institutionalized and sent back to the places they came from.
The remarks followed criticism of the president by the two lawmakers during his State of the Union address, in which he praised his administration's restrictive immigration policies and enforcement operations.
Omar has repeatedly said that she and her family face death threats, which she attributes to hateful political rhetoric, particularly statements made by Trump.
The security concerns have also been accompanied by physical attacks.
Last month, a Minnesota man was sentenced to 14 months in prison after being convicted of spraying Omar with vinegar during a public appearance.
The attacker, Anthony James Kazmierczak, acknowledged that he targeted the congresswoman because he disagreed with her progressive political views.
An extraordinary raid weeks before US elections
The search comes at a particularly sensitive moment in American politics, with congressional midterm elections scheduled for November 3.
The Justice Department traditionally follows guidelines intended to prevent investigative actions from improperly influencing elections, particularly when candidates for public office are involved.
CNN noted that searching the residence of a sitting member of Congress just weeks before an election is an exceptionally unusual step.
The operation also follows renewed attacks by Trump on other Muslim Democrats who have criticized Israel.
Last week, the president targeted Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic candidate for Michigan's US Senate seat, while endorsing his Republican opponent, Mike Rogers.
Trump described El-Sayed as a radical extremist and a sympathizer of terrorism. El-Sayed has also been an outspoken critic of Israel and has accused it of committing genocide in Gaza.
Omar's criticism of Israel and the 2019 entry ban
Omar has been among the most outspoken critics of Israel in the Democratic Party, taking positions that have repeatedly generated controversy both in Washington and Jerusalem.
Even before the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack and the subsequent war in Gaza, she supported the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions movement, known as BDS, which campaigns for economic and political pressure on Israel.
She has also compared Israel's treatment of Palestinians to South Africa's former apartheid system and accused Israel of genocide in Gaza.
During her first term in Congress, Omar faced criticism from members of her own party over statements about American support for Israel that many interpreted as antisemitic.
One particularly contentious episode involved her suggestion that American politicians supported Israel because of financial contributions from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, known as AIPAC.
In 2019, Israel barred Omar and Tlaib from entering the country, a decision that drew criticism even from prominent supporters of Israel within the Democratic Party.
Monday's search now places Omar at the center of another major political confrontation. Federal authorities have confirmed that a criminal investigation is underway, but have not disclosed its precise scope or announced charges against the congresswoman.

sources.news_title: Rep. Ilhan Omar's home raided in immigration investigation
sources.text:
Oct. 12 (UPI) — Federal agents raided Rep. Ilhan Omar’s Washington home on Monday as part of an ongoing immigration investigation.
Federal agents from Homeland Security Investigations descended upon the home of the Minnesota Democrat early on Monday morning, Fox News, ABC News and NBC News reported citing unnamed sources. The outlets said the investigation into Omar stems from her immigration paperwork.
“Today in the Washington, D.C., area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice,” a Justice Department spokesperson said in a statement. “This enforcement action is part of an ongoing investigation.”
The Justice Department added that the allegations against Omar are “criminal” in nature.
Omar is running for re-election on Nov. 3, as Democrats seek to win a majority in Congress.
There is not a law prohibiting federal law enforcement from taking actions against candidates so close to an election but the Justice Department has long been hesitant to do so as it may appear like election interference.
The Trump administration has been investigating claims of fraud in state social service programs in Minnesota. President Donald Trump claims that Somali immigrants have been behind widespread fraud in the state.
Border czar Tom Homan, who took over the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement operations in Minnesota earlier this year, said last month in a Fox News appearance that Omar was the subject of a Department of Homeland Security investigation.

sources.text:
Trump’s Vendetta Against Ilhan Omar Now Involves Federal Agents Raiding Her Home
Federal agents raided the home of Ilhan Omar on Monday, reportedly as part of an investigation into the congresswoman’s immigration paperwork.
The warranted search of Omar’s home in the Washington, D.C., area was conducted by the Department of Homeland Security. The search was first reported by Fox News. The Justice Department has noted that “Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice,” and that “enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal investigation,” but did not name Omar.
A spokesperson for Omar responded later on Monday. “This raid by Trump’s DHS is an outrageous abuse of power and an unprecedented escalation in the weaponization of federal law enforcement to target political enemies,” the spokesperson said, per NBC News. “For a decade, Donald Trump has relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Ilhan Omar with inflammatory rhetoric, repeatedly putting a target on her back. Now, those attacks have escalated to a pointless federal raid. The Congresswoman has done nothing wrong. No president should be able to use the power of the federal government to intimidate his political enemies.”
Omar herself responded, as well: “I’m OK,” she wrote. “Make no mistake: This is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement. For 10 years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced.”
Omar, a progressive Democrat who was born in Somalia, has become a favorite target of Trump, his administration, and MAGA politicians as they have sought to demonize Somali immigrants, particularly in the Minneapolis-St. Paul area, part of which Omar represents in Congress.
Trump called Omar “garbage” in December of last year, as his supporters chanted “Send her back,” and mocked Omar’s hijab at an event later the same month. “I love her. She comes in, does nothing but bitch,” the president continued. “She’s always complaining. She comes from her country, where I mean, it’s considered about the worst country in the world, right?” He then repeated an unsubstantiated claim that Omar married her brother. “She married her brother to get in,” Trump said. “Therefore, she’s here illegally. She should get the hell out. Throw her the hell out. She does nothing but complain.”
Earlier this year, Trump wrote that Omar is “low IQ,” “mentally deranged,” and “bad for our Country,” and that she — along with Rep. Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), who was born in Michigan, but like Omar is Muslim — should be sent “back from where they came — as fast as possible.”
Trump’s administration appears to be searching for a way to prosecute Omar, and to potentially deport her. Tom Homan, the White House border czar, told Fox News last month that Omar was the subject of an “ongoing criminal investigation” but declined to provide details. “If someone committed an immigration violation, if someone committed marriage fraud or anything like that, regardless if they’re a congressman or not, no one’s above the law,” he said. “So, I’ll leave it at that. We’ll let HSI, Homeland Security Investigations, continue the investigation.”
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin also said that Omar was being investigated last month, noting that “something is going to happen,” and claiming “we know she married her brother.”
However, the search of Omar’s apartment does not appear to be connected to the conspiracy theory about her brother, or supposed financial fraud. The New York Post reports that the investigation pertains to Omar’s immigration paperwork, which her father filled out when she was a child. Omar arrived in the United States from Somalia in 1995, when she was 12, and has been a U.S. citizen since 2000. She was first elected to Congress in 2018.
Trump last week posted a broader attack against Somalis in Minnesota, alleging they had “taken over” the state, which is now ridden with “Violence, Murder, and Mayhem.”
“The Somalis should not be allowed to get away with what they are doing,” the president wrote. “They view you as weak and stupid people. Fight back Minnesota, fight back!”
Omar responded on X. “Trump’s obsession with demonizing the Somali community is dangerous and reprehensible,” she wrote. “Hate to break it to him: Somali Minnesotans are resilient. We will not let Trump intimidate us. Our neighbors have our back.”

sources.text:
Federal agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar’s Washington home before dawn as part of a criminal investigation into her immigration paperwork, a probe she has long denied any wrongdoing in.
Homeland Security Investigations agents in HSI jackets were outside the Minnesota Democrat’s Washington, D.C., residence early Monday morning, starting around 6 a.m., after the Department of Justice secured a judicially authorized search warrant.
Fox News Digital reported the pre-dawn operation as part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation, with HSI and the Department of Homeland Security leading the action and the Justice Department involved.
A Department of Justice spokesperson confirmed the warrant in plain terms and later described the probe as criminal.
"Today in the Washington, D.C., area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice. This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal investigation,"
No arrests, charges, or inventory of seized items were announced. Fox News said it reached out to an Omar spokesperson; no on-record reply was quoted in the initial report.
Two sources close to the investigation told Fox the search grew from a criminal fraud inquiry into immigration paperwork Omar’s late father filled out when she was a child. The Justice Department’s public statement did not name that predicate in the quoted remarks.
The New York Post likewise framed the raid as tied to an ongoing DOJ criminal fraud investigation of those immigration documents, and noted that no formal charges have been filed.
Omar has denied long-running allegations that she entered under a false identity or took part in immigration fraud. Those claims remain allegations, not adjudicated findings, in the reporting provided.
Border czar Tom Homan said in mid-September that Omar was already subject to an ongoing “criminal” investigation, language that matches the Justice Department’s later description of Monday’s action.
That earlier posture tracks reporting on how Homan confirmed a criminal investigation even as Omar publicly disputed federal contact.
Breitbart noted that Vice President JD Vance had previously signaled the administration would look into immigration fraud allegations against Omar, which she has denied, and that she had not commented after the search.
Separate from the warrant, Omar has faced months of heat over financial disclosures. Her 2024 report listed her husband with assets between $6 million and $30 million. A 2025 filing revised shared assets to a maximum of $125,000, a multimillion-dollar drop, with lower estimates near $20,000 and debts in the tens of thousands, including student loans and credit card balances.
Reporting does not establish that those disclosure swings supplied the legal basis for Monday’s warrant. They do show a sitting member of Congress under sustained scrutiny on money and paperwork at the same time federal agents executed a criminal search at her home.
Legal background on the older marriage claims has already drawn close analysis of what proof would be required in any effort aimed at stripping citizenship over marriage fraud claims.
Public discussion of Omar has long included 2009-era allegations that she married her brother in an immigration scheme. A federal prosecutor has said the statute of limitations could hinder any investigation of that matter. Those claims remain disputed and unresolved in the material on hand.
Whether investigators can move from allegation to removal is a separate legal question that has already been examined in detail regarding limits on deportation over the brother-marriage allegation.
HSI is the principal investigative arm of DHS. Its portfolio covers cross-border crime, trafficking, smuggling, cybercrime, and counterterrorism support. A judicial warrant means a judge found probable cause for a search tied to a criminal case, not a press conference and not a conviction.
Omar has also pushed legislation to cut billions from ICE, the same broader homeland-security apparatus now executing process at her door, a record that produced swift conservative backlash over her ICE funding bill.
A search warrant is an investigative step. It is not an indictment. It is not a trial. As of the initial reporting, Omar faces no announced charges from this operation, and agents have released no public list of what they sought or took.
Still, the sequence is clear on the record that exists: Homan described a criminal investigation in mid-September; Vance flagged immigration-fraud scrutiny; DOJ secured a warrant; HSI carried it out at a member of Congress’s D.C. home before dawn; and sources close to the case point to childhood immigration paperwork filled out by her late father.
Minnesota politics around Omar already include a former trooper challenging her and tying Twin Cities disorder to Democratic leadership, a race covered as an ex-trooper challenge over Somali gang violence in the Twin Cities.
Voters can hold two thoughts at once. Due process applies to everyone, including a progressive star in the House. And equal enforcement means paperwork, marriage history, and financial disclosures get the same hard look whether the name on the file is famous or not.
When federal agents knock before sunrise on a congresswoman’s door, the country is entitled to facts, a clean process, and the same rules for the powerful that apply to everyone else.

sources.news_title: Ilhan Omar’s Home Raided by DHS Following Trump-GOP Deportation Threats
sources.text:
SUBSCRIBE TO OUR FREE NEWSLETTER
Daily news & progressive opinion—funded by the people, not the corporations—delivered straight to your inbox.
To donate by check, phone, or other method, see our More Ways to Give page.
Trump and other Republicans have called for Omar to be stripped of her citizenship and deported for years.
Following years of threats from President Donald Trump and other Republicans to deport Rep. Ilhan Omar, the Minnesota congresswoman's Washington, DC home was raided on Monday morning by agents with the Department of Homeland Security.
The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has confirmed that the raid was carried out as part of a judicially authorized warrant, which it said was part of an ongoing criminal investigation.
Fox News, which first reported news of the raid, said it was part of a probe into the naturalization paperwork filed by Omar's late father when she became a US citizen in 2000 after immigrating to the US as a refugee from Somalia in 1995.
In September, The New York Post reported that federal investigators were examining whether Omar may have been older than 17 when she obtained citizenship through her father as a minor in 2000. The allegation, which stems partly from a discrepancy in historical records of her birth year, has not been substantiated.
Aaron Reichlin-Melnick, a fellow at the American Immigration Council, argued that the case was "even weaker than it already seems," since federal immigration law includes a waiver for people who obtain legal status through fraud they were unaware of.
Joyce Vance, who served as the US attorney for the Northern District of Alabama under President Barack Obama, noted that the raid took place just weeks before the November 3 midterms, inside the 60-day window where DOJ typically avoids such dramatic actions.
"To state what’s obvious to prosecutors here, we are within the period before an election where DOJ doesn’t take overt steps in an investigation that might influence its outcome," she said, adding that it was "another hard norm out the window."
Omar has not yet commented on the raid as of Monday morning, and the DOJ has not indicated what, if any, specific charges have been filed against her.
The search comes after years of demands from Trump and other Republicans for Omar—who has served in the US House of Representatives since 2019—to be deported, imprisoned, or otherwise removed from office.
In a statement Monday morning, Joel Payne, a spokesperson for the progressive advocacy group MoveOn condemned the raid on Omar as a political attack.
“Rep. Omar is a dedicated public servant and a true ally for working families, and Donald Trump has done nothing but use racist tropes and stereotypes to attack her," he said. "Now, he’s abusing his power to physically intimidate and harass her."
Last November, Trump remarked that Omar should be thrown out of the country because she is "always complaining" and referenced her religious attire, referring to it as a "swaddling hijab." In another post that day, he called for the US to "denaturalize migrants who undermine domestic tranquility."
He also said Rep. Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), the only Palestinian American member of Congress, should be "sent back" along with Omar after the two protested his state of the Union address in February.
Trump has often referenced Omar while calling for all Somali immigrants to be deported from the country—even though most are US citizens. Trump has referred to Somalis collectively as "garbage" and said they have "low IQs."
Last week, Trump called for the people of Minnesota to "fight back" against Somalis living there in a post on Truth Social, which was widely interpreted as an incitement to violence.
In March, Vice President JD Vance said on a podcast that the administration believed Omar had "definitely committed immigration fraud against the United States of America" and that he'd discussed with senior Trump adviser Stephen Miller—who is not a federal prosecutor—how to "go after" her.
Beau Tremitiere, counsel and deputy director of impact programs for Protect Democracy, told Common Dreams that "raiding the home of a prominent critic and longtime target of President Trump’s racist attacks on the eve of an election is an obvious attempt to intimidate the opposition."
“This administration already has a long track record of failed political prosecutions," he said. "Each new one should both anger and stiffen the spine of those standing up for our democracy.”
Several Republican members of Congress have referenced Omar's religion and political viewpoints as reasons for her to be stripped of citizenship and deported.
Rep. Randy Fine (R-Fla.), who introduced a resolution to expel Omar from Congress last year, referred to her as a "Muslim terrorist" because of her outspoken criticism of Israel's genocide in Gaza and said she should not "be a citizen."
Rep. Brandon Gill (R-Texas) has also called for her deportation, claiming she helped to facilitate the "invasion" of the US after she discussed informing Somali American residents of her district of their constitutional rights should they encounter immigration officers.
In a statement Monday, House Democratic leadership called the raid on Omar's residence "deeply disturbing" and said it "raises serious questions about the continued corrupt weaponization of the federal government against Donald Trump’s adversaries."
"For years, Donald Trump and far-right extremists have relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Omar with vile personal attacks and baseless accusations," they said. "Now, less than 30 days until the midterm election, his violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family."
They added that "the American people deserve transparency, and we will deliver full accountability for the rogue abuse of power from the Department of Homeland Security and Department of Justice."
This article has been updated to include comments from House Democratic leadership and Beau Tremitiere at Protect Democracy.

sources.text:
WASHINGTON — Federal agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar's home on Oct. 12, according to an official familiar with the matter.
Homeland Security Investigations agents conducted the early-morning raid at the Democratic congresswoman's DC-area residence. The purpose for the search wasn't immediately clear, but top Trump administration officials, including Vice President JD Vance and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, have long accused the Minnesota lawmaker, who was born in Somalia and immigrated to the United States as a child refugee, of immigration fraud, which she denies.
The raid is a significant escalation of President Donald Trump's efforts to target his political opponents using the federal law enforcement apparatus. It also dramatically intensifies his years-long feud with Omar, a progressive Muslim whose religion and ethnicity Trump has frequently attacked.
People are also reading…
The Department of Homeland Security referred USA TODAY to the Justice Department for comment. In a statement, the DOJ confirmed Homeland Security Investigations had "executed a judicially authorized search warrant" at a Washington-area home as "part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation."
Spokespeople for Omar did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Who is Ilhan Omar?
Omar was elected in President Trump’s first term during a blue wave in 2018. She was an original member of the progressive group dubbed the "Squad," which also included Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Ayanna Pressley and Rashida Tlaib. She became the first Somali American in Congress.
She also immediately drew Trump's ire. In July 2019, the summer after she won her House seat, a North Carolina campaign rally crowd chanted "send her back" after Trump repeatedly criticized the congresswoman. Earlier this year, in January, Trump without evidence accused Omar of staging a town hall attack during which an attendee sprayed her with apple cider vinegar.
Omar has drawn controversy on her own, too. In 2019, she sparked bipartisan backlash for now-deleted tweets about Israel that sparked claims of antisemitism.
Her marriage history has also been a subject of scrutiny, dating back to her time as a state lawmaker. Online Minnesota court and marriage records show Omar was married to Ahmed Elmi in February 2009 before their divorce in December 2017. She then married Ahmed Hirsi, the father of her three children, in January 2018.
In 2016, she told Minnesota Public Radio she was legally married and physically separated from another man (seemingly Elmi) who was living in England but married Hirsi in a Muslim ceremony. She told MPR that it was "a difficult part of my personal history that I did not consider relevant in the context of a political campaign."
She legally divorced Hirsi in November 2019. She married lobbyist Tim Mynett in March 2020.

United States federal agents have searched the Washington, DC-area home of Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar, a vocal critic of President Donald Trump, as part of an ongoing criminal investigation.
Agents from Homeland Security Investigations carried out the search early Monday morning, according to The Associated Press news agency, citing two people familiar with the matter.

“I’m ok. Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement,” she wrote.
“For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation.”
“I will not be silenced,” she added.
The Somali-born congresswoman, who came to the US a child refugee and later became a naturalised citizen, represents a district in the state of Minnesota that includes Minneapolis.

Well, this is one knock at the door that a Squad press release cannot make disappear.
Federal investigators searched Rep. Ilhan Omar’s Washington home early Monday, bringing the investigation surrounding the progressive congresswoman out of the political shouting match and onto her doorstep. Agents wearing Homeland Security Investigations jackets were seen outside the residence, with the operation beginning around 6 a.m., according to reporting on the search.
“This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation,” the Justice Department said.
That is considerably more serious than another politician trading insults on television. DOJ confirmed that investigators executed a judicially authorized search warrant, although its public statement did not identify Omar or spell out the suspected offense.
Fox News, citing two sources close to the investigation, reported that the inquiry concerns alleged fraud involving immigration paperwork completed by Omar’s late father when she was a child. CBS also reported that its sources identified childhood immigration documents as the focus.
Here is the detail readers should keep their eyes on: the paperwork.
For years, the political fireworks have centered on allegations concerning Omar’s past marriage—allegations she has denied. Monday’s reporting points toward documents from her childhood instead. Those are different matters, however loudly people shout about them.
The Daily BS flagged that distinction last month while covering border czar Tom Homan’s confirmation of an investigation.
“I know things are going on, but I can’t give specifics of what’s happening,” Homan said in September. He also said “no one’s above the law.”
A useful principle. It should apply just as readily to a progressive congresswoman as to anybody else.
Omar’s side has hardly approached the controversy with quiet requests for clarification. AP reported that she has dismissed longstanding allegations as “disgusting lies.” Her chief of staff, Connor McNutt, responded to Vice President JD Vance’s accusations in March by calling them fabricated and defamatory—and branding Republicans the “pedophile protection party.”
There’s your elevated Washington discourse. Ask about alleged immigration fraud and get a political flamethrower in return.
That was an earlier statement, not a response to Monday’s search. Omar’s representatives did not immediately respond to requests for comment in the AP and Reuters reports reviewed for this draft.
Vance had described the administration’s position in May: “If we think that there’s a crime, we’re going to prosecute that crime.”
Now investigators have searched her home. What they found, what evidence supported the inquiry and whether prosecutors will bring charges remain unanswered publicly. The reporting reviewed for this draft did not announce an arrest or criminal charges.
A warrant does not establish guilt. But neither does an angry denial establish that investigators have nothing to examine. Both sides will have to live with what the evidence shows.
The search comes a little more than three weeks before the November 3 midterms, ensuring that every development lands in an already combustible political environment. The calendar invites scrutiny of the administration’s decisions. It does not give a member of Congress an automatic exemption from investigation.
The next question is straightforward: what do the documents say?
That answer will matter a great deal more than another round of name-calling from Capitol Hill.

I want the same standard for Omar that I want for everybody: show the evidence, follow the law and spare us the special treatment. A congressional pin is not a lifetime exemption from federal scrutiny.
Being a member of the Squad does not turn an investigation into persecution by definition. Prosecutors still have to make their case, and conservatives should demand evidence and accountability with the same conviction that we demand equal treatment.
Omar’s office reached for “pedophile protection party” when answering Vance. That is an ugly smear, and it deserves to be called one. It may thrill the faithful, but it answers precisely nothing about immigration paperwork.
If the allegations cannot be supported, prosecutors should say so. If the evidence supports charges, a congressional title should offer exactly zero protection.
