sources.news_title: Federal Agents Raid Rep. Ilhan Omar’s Washington-Area Home Amid Immigration Fraud Investigation
sources.text:
Homeland Security Investigations agents executed a court-authorized search warrant at Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar’s residence Monday as federal authorities continued examining allegations involving her immigration history, although the Justice Department has not announced criminal charges or publicly identified the evidence being sought.
By yourNEWS Media Newsroom
WASHINGTON — Federal agents searched the Washington-area residence of Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., early Monday, Oct. 12, as part of an ongoing criminal investigation, the Justice Department confirmed, marking a significant development in a federal inquiry that has drawn attention to the congresswoman’s immigration records and longstanding allegations disputed by Omar.
Agents from Homeland Security Investigations, the investigative division of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, carried out the search under a warrant authorized by a federal judge. The operation followed public statements from senior Trump administration officials indicating that federal authorities were examining potential irregularities involving the congresswoman’s immigration history.
The Justice Department confirmed the enforcement action but declined to identify the specific suspected offenses, the materials agents were seeking or whether Omar herself was the target of the investigation.
“Today in the Washington, D.C., area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice,” a department spokesperson said in a statement provided to Newsmax and other news organizations.
“This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal investigation.”
The Associated Press independently confirmed the search, citing people familiar with the operation who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to discuss an active investigation.
The agency reported that the Justice Department had not disclosed the investigation’s scope or the reasons investigators believed evidence relevant to the case might be found at Omar’s residence.
The New York Post reported Monday that the search was connected to a criminal fraud investigation concerning immigration documents submitted when Omar was a child. According to the newspaper, the inquiry involves paperwork completed by her late father during the family’s immigration process.
That reported focus has not been independently confirmed in the Justice Department’s public statement. Authorities also have not announced that Omar submitted fraudulent records or knowingly participated in any unlawful activity.
The distinction is significant because the execution of a search warrant does not establish that a crime occurred or that the occupant of the searched residence is guilty of wrongdoing.
Federal investigators generally must present sufficient information to establish probable cause before a judge authorizes a search. That legal standard concerns whether evidence connected to a suspected offense is likely to be found at a particular location. It is not equivalent to proof beyond a reasonable doubt, the standard required for a criminal conviction.
As of Monday morning, no criminal charges against Omar had been publicly announced in connection with the search.
Omar, 44, represents Minnesota’s 5th Congressional District, which includes Minneapolis and surrounding communities. First elected to the House of Representatives in 2018, she became one of the first two Muslim women elected to Congress and the first Somali American to serve in the House.
She has since become a prominent member of the progressive group of Democratic lawmakers commonly known as the Squad and a frequent critic of President Donald Trump’s immigration and domestic policies.
Her public disagreements with Trump have included disputes over immigration enforcement, refugee protections, government spending and the administration’s treatment of Minnesota’s Somali American community.
The latest federal action follows several weeks of renewed attention to Omar’s immigration history.
In September, the New York Post reported on federal scrutiny of records associated with her naturalization, including documents reportedly submitted by her father, Nur Said Mohamed Elmi.
Omar was born in Somalia and fled the country with her family during the civil war. After spending time in a refugee camp in Kenya, the family immigrated to the United States in the 1990s.
She became a naturalized American citizen in 2000 while still a teenager.
The circumstances of her family’s immigration and her subsequent acquisition of citizenship have periodically become subjects of political controversy, particularly among Republican critics who have questioned the accuracy of her immigration documentation.
The earlier Post reporting indicated that investigators were examining whether information provided during the family’s immigration and naturalization processes accurately reflected the applicants’ identities and backgrounds.
An individual’s naturalization record can include information concerning identity, age, residence, immigration status and other eligibility requirements.
Federal authorities may investigate deliberate misrepresentations in such records when they have evidence suggesting that material information was knowingly falsified.
However, discrepancies in historical paperwork do not automatically demonstrate fraud. Establishing a criminal violation generally requires proof of the relevant statutory elements, including any applicable knowledge, intent and materiality requirements.
The circumstances may be particularly complicated when immigration documents were submitted by a parent or guardian on behalf of a minor child.
Omar has maintained that she immigrated to the United States lawfully and has rejected allegations that her citizenship was obtained through fraud.
The September reporting also revived longstanding allegations concerning Omar’s former husband, Ahmed Elmi.
Republican critics have repeatedly alleged that Elmi was Omar’s brother and that their marriage was intended to facilitate immigration benefits.
Omar has consistently denied that claim, and it has not been established through a court finding or other publicly verified evidence.
The allegation has circulated for years in partisan political disputes, often alongside questions about Omar’s family relationships and marital history.
The New York Post’s September account, subsequently discussed by Newsmax, suggested that federal authorities were more likely to focus on immigration documentation than on the allegations concerning Omar’s former marriage.
The Justice Department has not publicly stated whether the marriage allegations are part of its current investigation.
The renewed scrutiny has been encouraged by senior administration officials, including White House border czar Tom Homan and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin.
In September, Homan publicly acknowledged that Omar was the subject of an ongoing criminal investigation.
He did not disclose the evidence investigators had gathered or announce any resulting charges.
Mullin subsequently discussed the matter during an interview with podcaster Benny Johnson, indicating that federal officials were examining allegations involving Omar’s immigration records and family background.
In the September interview circulated online, Mullin said he expected developments in the investigation.
“Something’s going to happen. This is an ongoing investigation. We know that she married her brother to try to bring him into the United States. We know he lives now in London,” Mullin told Johnson.
The secretary’s assertion concerning Omar’s marriage was presented as an allegation by an administration official. It has not been independently substantiated, and Omar has denied the underlying claim.
Mullin suggested that investigators were examining additional aspects of the family’s immigration history.
“There may be more to this—the whole family migration, and possibly some illegal activity for them to come to the United States to begin with. But all of this, we’re investigating,” he said.
The secretary emphasized that the department intended to establish whether criminal violations had occurred before pursuing enforcement action.
“Here’s what I want to make sure we do: if we actually move a case forward, it’s not a political case. It’s an actual case because they did things wrong.”
Mullin also described the broader immigration enforcement principles he said would guide investigations involving allegedly fraudulent applications.
“If you decided to break the law or lie on the information you gave to the United States—to be able to come into the United States, through either asylum or because you were just wanting to seek a better life—but you didn’t tell us who you actually were, you lied about certain things about your application.”
He continued by arguing that serious immigration-related misrepresentations could have consequences even when the underlying conduct occurred years earlier.
“Those things, there’s no expiration to that. If we can prove it then, that you shouldn’t have been here in the first place, we’ll deport you.”
That statement expressed the secretary’s enforcement position. Whether a particular criminal charge or civil action remains legally available depends on the applicable statute, limitations period and circumstances of the case.
Federal law establishes procedures under which citizenship obtained through naturalization may be revoked in certain circumstances, including when the government proves that naturalization was illegally procured or obtained through concealment of a material fact or willful misrepresentation.
Civil denaturalization proceedings are distinct from criminal prosecutions and involve different legal requirements.
Revocation of citizenship is not automatic following an allegation of immigration fraud, and government authorities must establish the legal basis for such action through the appropriate process.
In criminal cases, prosecutors must also address applicable statutes of limitations and prove the elements of any offense charged.
Even a successful denaturalization proceeding would not necessarily result in immediate deportation. Separate immigration procedures and applicable legal protections may determine whether removal is authorized.
The government has not announced any denaturalization proceedings against Omar.
Mullin said investigators were examining other cases in addition to the congresswoman’s immigration history.
“And so we’re looking at —it’s more than just her case. We’re looking at a lot of cases that are very similar to this, that we feel like there may have been fraud from the get-go,” he said.
The secretary again rejected the suggestion that the investigations should be understood as political retaliation.
“But when we move forward, it’s not political; it’s because you chose to break the nation’s laws.”
Those comments preceded Monday’s search and provide context for the administration’s public position, although they do not identify the evidence used to obtain the search warrant.
The operation itself was conducted by Homeland Security Investigations, a federal law enforcement agency whose responsibilities extend beyond routine immigration enforcement.
HSI investigates a broad range of offenses involving cross-border criminal activity, including immigration and document fraud, human trafficking, financial crimes, cybercrime, drug smuggling and certain national security threats.
Its agents may work with federal prosecutors and other law enforcement agencies when investigating conduct that falls within federal jurisdiction.
The agency’s involvement in Monday’s operation does not, by itself, establish which of those offenses investigators suspect.
Because federal authorities have not released the warrant or an accompanying affidavit, the precise legal justification for the search remains unknown publicly.
It is also unclear whether agents seized documents, computers, electronic devices or other materials during the operation.
Authorities have not identified additional locations searched in connection with the inquiry or announced whether other individuals are under investigation.
The operation represents an unusually prominent law enforcement action because it involved the residence of a sitting member of Congress.
Federal investigations involving lawmakers can raise significant questions concerning the separation of powers and protections associated with legislative activity.
The Constitution’s Speech or Debate Clause protects members of Congress from being questioned in other branches of government about certain legitimate legislative acts.
That protection does not provide general immunity from criminal investigations or prosecution for conduct unrelated to legislative responsibilities.
Whether the clause becomes relevant to a particular search depends on the materials sought, the nature of the investigation and any disputes concerning legislative records or communications.
The Justice Department has not publicly described how the warrant was structured or whether special procedures were used to protect potentially privileged material.
The search also arrives during an increasingly contentious period in relations between the Trump administration and Omar.
The congresswoman has repeatedly criticized federal immigration operations in Minnesota and challenged administration policies involving refugees, asylum seekers and deportations.
Trump, in turn, has frequently singled out Omar in public statements, questioning her political positions and criticizing her role in Congress.
Omar has described repeated attacks on her immigration history as discriminatory and politically motivated.
Supporters of the congresswoman have argued that scrutiny of her background has often relied on allegations that were never substantiated.
Administration officials maintain that federal investigators have a responsibility to examine credible allegations of immigration fraud regardless of the political position of the individuals involved.
The timing of Monday’s search, approximately three weeks before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, is likely to draw additional attention to the investigation.
Omar is seeking another term representing Minnesota’s 5th District, where she has maintained strong support among progressive and Democratic voters.
The search occurred while congressional candidates across the country were entering the final weeks of campaigning, making any law enforcement development involving a sitting member of Congress particularly significant.
However, the timing alone does not establish that investigators acted for political reasons. Similarly, the existence of a judicially authorized search warrant does not establish that the allegations against Omar are true.
The two questions — whether investigators possess sufficient evidence to pursue a criminal case and whether the investigation has been conducted independently of political considerations — require separate examination.
Federal prosecutors operate under Justice Department policies intended to protect the integrity of investigations and prevent improper interference in electoral processes.
Those principles are particularly relevant in cases involving public officials, where law enforcement actions can carry political consequences even before criminal charges are filed.
The Justice Department has not explained whether special review procedures were applied before authorizing the search.
The Associated Press reported that Omar’s representatives had been contacted for comment but had not immediately provided a response to the agency’s inquiry.
Other news organizations reported similar difficulties obtaining an immediate statement from the congresswoman’s office.
Omar’s position on the longstanding allegations involving her immigration history is well established: She has denied wrongdoing and rejected claims that her past marriage was part of an immigration fraud scheme.
The current investigation has not resulted in a public criminal indictment, and no court has determined that her citizenship was obtained unlawfully.
Additional information may emerge if prosecutors file charges, seek further judicial action or release documents associated with the warrant.
For now, Monday’s confirmed developments are limited to the execution of a federal search warrant at Omar’s Washington-area residence and the Justice Department’s acknowledgment that the operation was part of an ongoing criminal investigation.
The reported connection to immigration fraud allegations rests on information attributed to sources familiar with the matter, while the government has declined to publicly identify the allegations supporting the search.
The case places renewed attention on Omar’s immigration history, the administration’s enforcement priorities and the legal standards governing investigations of elected officials.
Any subsequent prosecution would require federal authorities to establish specific violations through evidence and applicable judicial procedures, while Omar would retain the constitutional protections afforded to anyone accused of a crime.

sources.news_title: Federal officers carry out search at Minnesota Rep. Ilhan Omar’s DC-area home
sources.text:
(CNN) — Federal officers executed a search warrant early Monday at the Washington, DC-area home of Rep. Ilhan Omar, the Minnesota Democrat who has been the persistent target of ire from President Donald Trump’s administration, according to a Justice Department spokesperson and a source familiar with the matter.
The congresswoman is running for reelection, and the search warrant was executed only weeks before the midterms.
It is unusual for the Justice Department to take such an aggressive investigative step toward a candidate so close to an election. Voting is well underway in Minnesota, with more than 127,000 people having already voted, according to data from the secretary of state.
The Department of Justice said in a statement Monday that investigators from Homeland Security Investigations, a branch of the Department of Homeland Security that handles criminal investigations, “executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice.”
“This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation,” a DOJ spokesperson said.
The statement did not indicate what the investigation entailed.
Omar called the search “the latest escalation” in Trump’s “campaign of political intimidation.”
“I’m ok. Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement,” she wrote on X. “For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced.”
House Democratic leaders called the search “deeply disturbing” and said it “raises serious questions about the continued corrupt weaponization of the federal government against Donald Trump’s adversaries.”
“For years, Donald Trump and far-right extremists have relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Omar with vile personal attacks and baseless accusations,” House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, Whip Katherine Clark and caucus Chair Pete Aguilar said in a statement, adding that it comes with “less than 30 days until the midterm election.”
“The American people deserve transparency, and we will deliver full accountability for the rogue abuse of power from the Department of Homeland Security and Department of Justice,” the statement added.
A spokesperson for the congresswoman said in a statement to CNN, “For a decade, Donald Trump has relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Ilhan Omar with inflammatory rhetoric, repeatedly putting a target on her back. Now, those attacks have escalated to a pointless federal raid. The Congresswoman has done nothing wrong.”
While authorities have not said what prompted the search, administration officials have previously indicated that Omar was facing an investigation.
White House border czar Tom Homan said on Fox News last month that “things are going on” in relation to Omar, before adding: “But I can’t give the specifics of what’s happening.”
Speaking to Fox on Monday morning, Homan confirmed the search warrant was executed, but provided no other information.
“The specifics of the investigation, I think I need to turn that over to Todd Blanche or Markwayne Mullin,” he said, referring to the attorney general and DHS secretary. “I don’t want to get ahead of them commenting on an ongoing investigation.”
One of Omar’s neighbors told CNN they were awoken around 4:30 a.m. Monday to the sounds of banging on doors. Later that morning, CNN observed that the home was surrounded by Homeland Security Investigations officers and that investigators were removing boxes from the home. Before leaving the scene, officials used a camera to document the condition of the house.
Omar was born in Somalia and grew up at the peak of that country’s civil war. She fled to the US as a teenager and later became a US citizen. She was first elected to Congress in 2018 and became part of “The Squad,” a group of congresswomen of color known for pushing for progressive causes.
Since joining Congress, she has been the target of racist vitriol, including from Trump, who called Omar “garbage” last year and said Somalis should “go back to where they came from.”
Omar’s home district in Minnesota was the target of an expansive immigration-enforcement campaign earlier this year that led to violent clashes between protesters and immigration authorities and the fatal shootings of two US citizens.
Top administration officials, including Homeland Security Secretary Mullin, have accused Omar of marrying her brother to help bring him into the United States. They have provided no proof of this claim.
Homan said on Fox News last month, referencing Omar, that if “someone committed immigration violation, someone committed marriage fraud, or anything like that, regardless if they’re a congressman or not, no one’s above the law.”
Asked specifically whether that means there was an open investigation into Omar, Homan responded: “I’m confirming that ICE is — yeah, like I said months ago, that is something that’s been reported and needs to be looked at.”
In prior years, the department has treaded cautiously for the 60-day period before an Election Day to not make searches or levy charges that would disadvantage a candidate. Department policy also bars prosecutors and investigative agents from selecting timing in an investigation so that it would influence an election.
Top Justice Department leadership signed off on the search after thorough deliberations given the proximity to the election, and a federal judge ultimately approved it, a source familiar with the investigation told CNN on Monday.
The Justice Department also has special policies requiring additional approvals when investigations involve a member of Congress, and the Constitution provides additional protections for members around papers and communications that relate to their legislative work.
This story has been updated with additional information.

sources.news_title: Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home searched by federal agents in criminal probe
sources.text:
Federal agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home in Washington, D.C., on Monday morning, according to two people familiar with the investigation.
One of the people familiar with the probe said the search is part of a yearslong criminal investigation by Homeland Security Investigations, the U.S. attorney in Minneapolis and the Justice Department. The probe, which involves whistleblowers, documents and witness testimony, deals partly with immigration and fraud, but it goes beyond those things, the source said.
A Justice Department spokesperson said in a statement that Homeland Security Investigations “executed a judicially authorized search warrant” as “part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation.”
The statement did not specify that the warrant was related to Omar, D-Minn., or provide further information about the nature of the investigation.
In a post on X, Omar called the search “an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement,” adding that over the last decade, President Donald Trump “has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced.”
Trump has frequently lashed out at Omar, who is a member of a progressive faction of women in Congress collectively known as the “squad,” criticizing her over her liberal positions and saying she should “go back” to where she came from.
Asked about the search Monday, Trump told reporters he had “nothing to do with it,” adding that investigators were “looking at her very carefully.”
“I’ve always found her to be totally crooked, personally, but that has nothing to do with me,” Trump said. “I think she’s a terrible person, but that’s really up to the DOJ.”
House Democratic leaders said in a joint statement that the search was “deeply disturbing and raises serious questions about the continued corrupt weaponization of the federal government against Donald Trump’s adversaries.”
Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York, Minority Whip Katherine Clark of Massachusetts and Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar of California vowed in the statement to “deliver full accountability for the rogue abuse of power from the Department of Homeland Security and Department of Justice.”
The search was first reported by Fox News. The White House and the Department of Homeland Security referred questions about the search to the Justice Department.
Omar, who is running for re-election, immigrated to the U.S. from the war-torn country of Somalia as a child in the 1990s.
The timing of Monday’s search puts it under added scrutiny: There are 22 days until the midterm elections, and a long-standing Justice Department practice tells prosecutors to be especially careful about actions near an election that could appear to help or hurt a candidate.
There is no blanket rule barring the department from acting within 60 days before an election, but that has long been an unwritten practice. The written policy says prosecutors and agents cannot time investigative steps or public statements to influence an election and directs them to seek guidance when the timing could raise questions.
That guidance is not always followed. In 2016, then-FBI Director James Comey publicly disclosed developments in the email probe of Democratic presidential nominee Hillary Clinton just 11 days before the presidential election.
After he took office, Trump fired Comey, and the administration justified his dismissal by saying he had violated long-standing principles of the Justice Department by announcing his conclusions about the Clinton case. Trump said he would have fired Comey “regardless” of the Justice Department memo outlining what it said were his missteps.
Early in Trump’s second term, Justice Department officials used the prospect of election interference as a basis to throw out a corruption case against former New York Mayor Eric Adams in federal court in Manhattan. Adams’ indictment on charges of bribery and campaign finance violations was filed about a year before the 2025 mayoral election, during former President Joe Biden’s tenure.
But under Trump, then-acting Deputy Attorney General Emil Bove moved in February 2025 to dismiss the case, writing that the move was necessary in part because of “risks of interference” with the city’s upcoming elections — a highly controversial push that led to the resignation of the acting U.S. attorney overseeing the matter.
Late last month, the Justice Department’s Office of the Inspector General recommended that the department’s leaders prioritize giving guidance to agents and prosecutors about actions that could “foreseeably affect an impending election.”
Those include “the taking of overt investigative steps, indictments, public announcements, or other actions” that could have such an impact, according to the recommendation, which was initially part of a 2018 report on the Justice Department and the FBI’s actions leading up to the 2016 election.
Last month, border czar Tom Homan told Fox News that DHS was investigating Omar.
“If someone committed immigration violation, if someone committed marriage fraud or anything like that, regardless if they’re a congressman or not, no one’s above the law,” Homan said at the time. “So I’ll leave it at that. We’ll let HSI, Homeland Security Investigations, continue the investigation.”
Omar fled Somalia’s civil war with her family when she was 8 years old and stayed in a Kenyan refugee camp for four years before she moved to the U.S., her website details.
Ahead of Monday’s news, Trump again targeted both Omar and Somalis over the weekend in his remarks at a rally in Tennessee.
“How about Ilhan Omar? She comes from Somalia,” he said Saturday as the crowd booed.
Trump went on to characterize the country as ungoverned and lawless, saying, “All they have is crime and squalor.”
“What they’ve done to Minnesota, these people from Somalia, what they’ve done to Minnesota should never be allowed,” he added. “And let’s see what happens. JD Vance and our people are looking at it very strongly.”
Early this year, Trump said the Justice Department and Congress are “looking at” the congresswoman. He has also repeatedly targeted Minnesota over fraud scandals that roiled the state.
Last week, Trump told Minnesotans to “fight back” against Somali immigrants, claiming on Truth Social that the state “is being taken over by Somali Immigrants.”
One of the highest-profile fraud cases alleged the theft of $250 million from a Covid-related program that provided food for children. Since then, the Justice Department has announced criminal charges against more than a dozen people in Minnesota over allegations of social services fraud.
The former leader of Feeding Our Future, the nonprofit at the center of the $250 million fraud case, is white. Most of the defendants in the related cases are of Somali descent, according to the U.S. attorney’s office, a fact Trump has highlighted as he has repeatedly disparaged people of Somali descent.
Omar blamed Trump’s rhetoric about her and Somali immigrants as a contributing factor in an attack on her at a town hall event in January.

sources.news_title: U.S. launches immigration raid of Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home as part of criminal probe
sources.text:
U.S. authorities conducted a pre-dawn raid on Monday on the Washington-area home of Democratic U.S. Representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota, an outspoken critic of Donald Trump who has been the target of political insults by the Republican president, as part of an ongoing investigation, the Justice Department said.
A person familiar with the investigation said it is related to alleged immigration fraud, and part of the probe concerns the Somali-born lawmaker’s immigration paperwork, which was filled out by her late father when she was a child.
Omar wrote in a social media post that the U.S. government is being weaponized to target a political enemy of the president.
“For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns,” Omar said. “This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced.”
Other Democrats accused Trump and his administration of abuse of power. Omar, 44, is seeking a fifth two-year term in the U.S. House of Representatives in the midterm elections on November 3.
In announcing the raid, a Justice Department spokesperson said: “Today in the Washington, DC area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice. This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal investigation.”
Homeland Security Investigations is part of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, or ICE.
Tom Homan, the Trump administration’s border czar, told Fox Business Network that the Justice Department is leading the investigation with the Department of Homeland Security. Homan declined to get into the specifics of an ongoing criminal investigation.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, a Trump appointee, said last month that “something’s gonna happen” in the investigation into Omar’s family’s entry into the United States.
“If we can prove that you shouldn’t have been here in the first place, we’ll deport you,” Mullin told conservative podcaster Benny Johnson at the time.
Monday’s raid was carried out a little more than three weeks before the midterms, with Trump’s party seeking to retain control of Congress. Omar, a prominent progressive, represents a safe Democratic district. She won re-election in 2024 by a margin of 50 percentage points.
Democrats condemn raid
In a joint statement, U.S. House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries and other members of the party’s leadership in the chamber said the raid was “deeply disturbing and raises serious questions about the” weaponization of the federal government against Trump’s enemies.
Republicans have “relentlessly targeted” Omar, said Jeffries, joined by Representatives Katherine Clark and Pete Aguilar. Trump’s “mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family,” they added, and they vowed to “deliver full accountability” for what they called a “rogue abuse of power.”
Minnesota Democrats also condemned the raid.
“Americans see this for what it is,” Minnesota Governor Tim Walz, a Democrat, wrote on social media. “President Trump is abusing his power to go after political opponents weeks before an election.”
Few Republican lawmakers publicly commented. One who did, Representative Nancy Mace, wrote online: “If the fraud is proven, she should be denaturalized and removed from this country. NO ONE is above the law.”
Justice Department policy bars federal prosecutors and agents from timing any action to affect an election’s outcome or benefit a candidate or party. It historically has avoided taking investigative steps against political candidates within about 60 days of an election.
George Washington University law professor Randall Eliason, a former U.S. public corruption prosecutor, said the raid appears to be a break with past Justice Department practice of avoiding investigative steps likely to become public close to Election Day. But Eliason noted there is no way of enforcing the policy.
“The idea is to avoid even the appearance of any kind of interference by the Department of Justice with the political process,” Eliason said. “It’s not surprising that they wouldn’t really care about violating this policy because they’ve shown they don’t really care about politicizing the Justice Department in many other ways.”
A person familiar with the investigation said the Justice Department consulted with its Public Integrity Section, a unit that has historically advised and approved investigations of members of Congress, and acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter prior to the search. The Trump administration has reduced the Public Integrity Section to about two lawyers and curtailed much of its authority.
Investigations of Trump critics
The Justice Department during Trump’s second term in office has investigated and brought charges against a range of Trump’s perceived political enemies.
It has charged former FBI Director James Comey, New York state Attorney-General Letitia James and Trump’s former national security adviser turned critic John Bolton. It also has investigated Democratic lawmakers who urged the U.S. military not to follow illegal orders, Democratic Senator Adam Schiff and Federal Reserve officials Jerome Powell and Lisa Cook.
The case against James and one of two brought against Comey were thrown out by a federal judge. Bolton pleaded guilty and is scheduled to be sentenced later this month. Grand juries and federal judges have stymied several other probes.
Omar has faced political insults from Trump, who has cast the Somali American community as a threat to Minnesota in a burst of anti-Somali and anti-Muslim rhetoric. Omar has called Trump’s focus on her an “unhealthy and creepy obsession.”
Civil rights advocates have criticized Trump’s rhetoric toward minorities and immigrants, including when he previously called Somalis “garbage.”
Trump in February said that Omar and Democratic Representative Rashida Tlaib of Michigan, who is also Muslim, should be “institutionalized” and sent back to “where they came from.” Both lawmakers had criticized Trump during his State of the Union address as he touted his administration’s hard-line immigration crackdown and its immigration enforcement actions.
Omar has said she and her family have faced death threats, which she attributes to “hateful political rhetoric,” especially from Trump.
Last month, a Minnesota man who squirted vinegar on Omar was sentenced to one year and two months in prison after pleading guilty to assaulting a federal official. Anthony James Kazmierczak admitted to attacking Omar because he disagreed with her progressive political views.

sources.news_title: Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar's DC home, DOJ says it approved the warrant
sources.text:
Federal agents searched the Washington, D.C. home of Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., Monday morning.
The Department of Justice said in a statement to NPR that agents with Homeland Security Investigations "executed a judicially authorized search warrant."
The warrant was approved by the DOJ and is part of an "ongoing federal investigation." Federal authorities did not give further details on the reason for the probe.
Details about the investigation were confirmed by current and former federal officials with knowledge of the search who were not authorized to speak publicly.
One current official said this search is part of a multi-year probe that includes whistleblower complaints. A former official, who had previously been briefed on the matter, said the investigation deals with immigration fraud allegations.
Omar criticized the search on social media.
"Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement," Omar posted on social media. "I will not be silenced."
Several HSI agents could be seen walking near and around Omar's home on Monday.
Jackie Rogers, a spokesperson for the congresswoman, called the search an "outrageous abuse of power and an unprecedented escalation in the weaponization of federal law enforcement to target political enemies."
Sharon Jackson, 79, lives across the street from the congresswoman and said federal agents woke her up around 4:30 a.m. Monday morning.
"I got awakened by boom, boom, boom," Jackson said. "They were out here with a great big truck."
The search took place ahead of next month's midterm elections, in which Omar is seeking reelection.
Vice President Vance has previously alleged Omar committed immigration fraud — something she denies.

In recent history, the Justice Department's practice has been to advise prosecutors not to take any overt investigative steps against members of Congress or candidates within 60 days of an election. The midterm elections, during which Omar is up for reelection, take place in 22 days, with early voting starting in Minnesota later this week.

Omar released a statement on social media on Monday, saying she is "ok" and that the search at her residence is "an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement."
"I will not be silenced," she wrote in the statement.
It's unclear whether Omar was at her D.C.-area residence at the time of Monday's search.
White House border czar Tom Homan confirmed the investigation in an interview with Fox News on Monday, but offered few details. Homan said he didn't want to get ahead of Attorney General Todd Blanche on any matter related to the investigation.

JD Vance and our people are looking at it very strongly," Trump said during a rally on Saturday.
In social media posts earlier this year, Trump also said Omar "should be in jail" and "sent back to Somalia."
Trump's remarks directed at Omar have drawn criticism, and Omar said earlier this year that Trump's rhetoric has led threats against her to "skyrocket."
The White House referred all comment requests to the Department of Justice.
Vice President JD Vance, who the administration has tasked with leading the so-called "anti-fraud efforts" said during a White House briefing in May that the administration was going to look into Omar for immigration fraud allegations.
Omar has previously denied any wrongdoing and has not been charged with a crime.

Fox News reports that HSI agents arrived at Omar’s D.C. home around 6 a.m. Eastern. Citing a source familiar with the matter, the outlet says the search stems from a criminal fraud investigation involving immigration paperwork completed by Omar’s late father when she was a child.
Fox also reports that two sources confirmed details of the probe after White House border czar Tom Homan said in September that Omar was the subject of an ongoing criminal investigation. Omar later said federal officials had not contacted her and dismissed the matter as a political attack.

BREAKING: Federal agents searched Minnesota Rep. Ilhan Omar's home as part of a criminal investigation, AP sources say. https://t.co/67uyHWqjY9
— The Associated Press (@AP) October 12, 2026
The Associated Press reports that multiple people familiar with the matter identified Omar’s home as the target of the Monday-morning search and HSI as the agency that conducted it. Those sources spoke anonymously because the investigation remains active.

Omar, a Minnesota Democrat and prominent member of the far-left “Squad,” has represented the state’s 5th Congressional District since 2019. Her office had not publicly explained the search when the first reports appeared Monday morning.
A federal search warrant is not a criminal conviction, and no charge or arrest had been announced in the initial reporting. It does mean investigators persuaded a judge that probable cause existed to authorize a search for evidence at the specified location.

sources.news_title: Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home in criminal probe, AP sources say
sources.text:
WASHINGTON — Federal agents on Monday searched the home of Democratic U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar, a startling escalation in a criminal investigation that brings renewed scrutiny to the frequent target of Trump administration derision in the final weeks of her reelection bid.
The search of the Minnesota congresswoman's home so close to next month's midterm contests that will determine control of the House and the Senate was swiftly condemned by top Democrats in Congress, who raised questions about the timing given longstanding Justice Department protocol to avoid overt investigative steps involving political candidates in the direct run-up to an election.
The Justice Department confirmed in a statement that Homeland Security Investigations agents executed a judicially authorized search warrant in the Washington, D.C., area in connection with an ongoing federal criminal investigation but provided no other details.
The nature and scope of the investigation were unclear, though officials in President Donald Trump's administration have repeatedly hinted at the existence of an inquiry targeting Omar, a Somali-born Democrat whose status as an immigrant to the U.S. and left-wing views have repeatedly drawn criticism from Republicans and senior Trump officials.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said last month that there was an "ongoing investigation" related in part to whether Omar lied on her immigration forms and that "something's going to happen."
Omar responded to the search with a statement on X that called it an "attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement."
"For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation," she said. "I will not be silenced."
Though the Republican focus on Omar's background dates back years, the search of her home took place three weeks before the November midterms, in which Omar is on the ballot for reelection. The Justice Department has historically sought to avoid public investigative actions involving a candidate within 60 days of a primary or general election.
"For years, Donald Trump and far-right extremists have relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Omar with vile personal attacks and baseless accusations," top House Democratic leaders said in a statement. "Now, less than 30 days until the midterm election, his violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family."
Trump as recently as this past weekend brought up Omar at a rally in Tennessee, where he attacked her upbringing and suggested that Vice President JD Vance "and our people" were investigating her.
Vance has in the past accused Omar of committing immigration fraud — an allegation she has denied — and has said he and a top White House official were trying to figure out how to investigate her.
A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security, of which Homeland Security Investigations is part, referred questions about the search to the Justice Department. The Justice Department said in a statement that Monday's enforcement action "is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation."
The street was blocked off Monday morning as HSI agents remained near the home.
Omar, who was first elected to the House in 2018, represents Minnesota's 5th District, including Minneapolis. She is part of The Squad of progressive lawmakers who are a vibrant political force on the left wing of Congress but have also endured repeated attacks from Trump, dating back to his first term. She was one of the first two Muslim-American women in the House and the first African refugee to be elected to Congress.
When Republicans swept control of the House in 2023, they voted to oust Omar from the House Foreign Affairs Committee, citing her anti-Israel remarks.

sources.news_title: US agents raid congresswoman Omar’s home over immigration paperwork probe
sources.text:
US federal agents on Monday searched the Washington, DC-area home of Minnesota Congresswoman Ilhan Omar as part of an ongoing criminal investigation, according to reports by the New York Post and Associated Press.
The Department of Homeland Security’s Homeland Security Investigations unit carried out the search under a warrant authorised by a court, the Department of Justice said.
“Today in the Washington, D.C. area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice,” a DOJ spokesperson told Fox News Digital, according to the New York Post report published on Monday, October 12, 2026.
“This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal investigation,” the spokesperson added.
The New York Post reported that the investigation concerned alleged fraud involving the Democratic congresswoman’s immigration paperwork.
However, the Justice Department did not publicly provide further details about the investigation in its statement.
The Associated Press also reported that federal agents searched Omar’s home on Monday morning as part of a criminal investigation, citing people familiar with the matter.
It said the Justice Department confirmed the execution of the warrant but did not disclose additional information about the case.
Omar, 44, represents Minnesota’s 5th Congressional District, which includes Minneapolis.
She was first elected to the US House of Representatives in 2018 and is known for her progressive political views and criticism of President Donald Trump.
The investigation remains ongoing, and the available reports do not establish that Omar has been charged with a crime in connection with the case.

sources.news_title: US Congresswoman Ilhan Omar's home raided in DOJ immigration probe
sources.text:
US authorities conducted a predawn raid on Monday on the Washington-area home of Democratic US Representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota, as part of an ongoing investigation, the US Justice Department said.
A person familiar with the investigation said it is related to alleged immigration fraud, and part of the probe concerns the Somali-born lawmaker's immigration paperwork, which was filled out by her late father when she was a child.
Omar claimed in a social media post that the US government is being weaponized to target a political enemy of the US president.
"For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns," Omar said. "This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced."
Trump denies involvement in Omar investigation
US President Donald Trump denied involvement in the investigation when asked about Omar on Monday. “I understand they’re looking at her very carefully,” he said, calling her “totally crooked” and “a terrible person.” He added, “That’s really up to the DOJ — I have nothing to do with it.”
Omar, 44, is seeking a fifth two-year term in the US House of Representatives in the midterm elections on November 3.
In announcing the raid, a Justice Department spokesperson said: "Today in the Washington, DC area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice. This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal investigation."
Homeland Security Investigations is part of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
Tom Homan, the Trump administration's border czar, told Fox Business Network that the Justice Department is leading the investigation with the Department of Homeland Security. Homan declined to get into the specifics of an ongoing criminal investigation.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, a Trump appointee, said last month that "something's gonna happen" in the investigation into Omar's family's entry into the United States.
"If we can prove that you shouldn't have been here in the first place, we'll deport you," Mullin told conservative podcaster Benny Johnson at the time.
Monday's raid was carried out a little more than three weeks before the midterms, with Trump's party seeking to retain control of Congress. Omar, a prominent progressive, represents a safe Democratic district. She won reelection in 2024 by a margin of 50 percentage points.
Democrats condemn raid on Omar's home
In a joint statement, US House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries and other members of the party's leadership in the chamber said the raid was "deeply disturbing and raises serious questions about the" weaponization of the federal government against Trump's enemies.
Republicans have "relentlessly targeted" Omar, said Jeffries, joined by Representatives Katherine Clark and Pete Aguilar. sources.text:
Trump critic Ilhan Omar's Washington DC home raided in immigration fraud probe
US federal agents raided Trump critic Ilhan Omar's Washington, DC, home early Monday as part of an immigration fraud probe, with multiple agents wearing Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) jackets seen outside the property, according to local media.
US Federal agents searched the home of Democratic Congresswoman Ilhan Omar on Monday as part of a criminal investigation. The search was carried out by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) under a judicially authorised warrant in Washington, DC, according to the US Justice Department, although authorities have not publicly disclosed the full details of the case.
The raid centres on allegations involving Omar's immigration paperwork, which sources cited by Fox News Digital said had been completed by her late father when she was a child. However, the Justice Department has confirmed only that agents executed a search warrant as part of an ongoing federal investigation. The precise allegations, evidence gathered and any potential charges have not been publicly established.
The development is particularly significant because Omar, a Somali-born American lawmaker and outspoken critic of Trump, has repeatedly clashed with the US President over immigration, allegations of fraud and his treatment of Somali Americans. Trump has publicly accused her of wrongdoing, while Omar has accused him of using such allegations to target political opponents and stoke hostility towards immigrant communities.
WHAT WE KNOW ABOUT THE RAID
Multiple agents wearing HSI jackets were seen outside Omar's Washington home in the early hours of Monday, according to local media.
A Justice Department spokesperson confirmed the operation to Fox News, saying: "Today in the Washington, DC, area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorised search warrant secured by the Department of Justice. This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal investigation."
HSI is the investigative arm of the Department of Homeland Security. It investigates a wide range of alleged crimes, including human trafficking, drug smuggling, cybercrime and cross-border criminal activity. The investigation into Omar had already attracted attention in September, when White House border official Tom Homan confirmed that she was the subject of an ongoing criminal investigation.
However, Omar had said federal authorities had not contacted her about the matter. "No, they have not," she said when asked whether officials had reached out to her. She dismissed the claims as right-wing attacks, according to Fox News. The latest search marks a significant development in the case. However, a search warrant does not establish that a person has committed a crime, and no charges against Omar have been confirmed in the reports available.
OMAR ACCUSES TRUMP OF POLITICAL INTIMIDATION
Hours later, she reassured her supporters in a statement on X, accusing Trump of using federal law enforcement to target his political opponents. "I'm ok," she wrote, describing the raid as the latest escalation in what she called a decade-long campaign of "baseless lies and smear campaigns".
"I will not be silenced," she added.
TRUMP AND OMAR'S FEUD OVER FRAUD ALLEGATIONS
The investigation has unfolded against the backdrop of an increasingly bitter dispute between Trump and Omar, one of the most prominent progressive Democrats in Congress. Their conflict has frequently centred on immigration, race, national identity and allegations of fraud involving Minnesota's Somali American community.
In May, Trump called Omar "crooked as hell" while discussing alleged fraud in Minnesota. The US President has also revived allegations concerning Omar's immigration and marital history, claims she has disputed.
Omar responded in a June 2 opinion article published by The Guardian, accusing Trump of using fraud allegations to attack her and the Somali American community. "Any keen observer will recognize the pattern of inciting hostility against me and the Somali community whenever his own failures and corruption catches up to him," she wrote.
She also accused the president of hypocrisy, arguing that his administration's approach to alleged fraud was politically motivated. Omar has maintained that wrongdoing should be investigated and prosecuted, but has criticised what she describes as the selective use of anti-fraud campaigns against political opponents and minority communities.
The dispute has become part of a broader confrontation between the Trump administration and progressive Democrats over immigration enforcement. Omar has been particularly vocal in opposing the administration's crackdown on immigrants and its policies towards Somali Americans.
In September, she introduced the Make ICE Pay Act, legislation intended to redirect funding allocated to Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection towards communities affected by federal immigration operations.
WHO IS ILHAN OMAR?
Omar represents Minnesota's 5th Congressional District and was first elected to the US House of Representatives in 2018. She is a prominent member of the progressive group informally known as the Squad, whose members have advocated policies including expanded healthcare access and changes to US immigration enforcement.
Born in Somalia, Omar came to the US as a refugee during her childhood and later became a US citizen. Her background has repeatedly featured in political attacks against her, particularly from Trump and his allies.

Federal Agents Raid Minnesota Rep. Ilhan Omar’s D.C. Home In Criminal Probe
Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home as part of a criminal investigation, AP sources say – WTOP News
sources.text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Federal agents on Monday searched the home of Democratic U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar, a startling escalation in a criminal investigation that brings renewed scrutiny to the frequent target of Trump administration derision in the final weeks of her reelection bid.
The search of the Minnesota congresswoman’s home so close to next month’s midterm contests that will determine control of the House and the Senate was swiftly condemned by top Democrats in Congress, who raised questions about the timing given longstanding Justice Department protocol to avoid overt investigative steps involving political candidates in the direct run-up to an election.
The Justice Department confirmed in a statement that Homeland Security Investigations agents executed a judicially authorized search warrant in the Washington, D.C., area in connection with an ongoing federal criminal investigation but provided no other details.
The nature and scope of the investigation were unclear, though officials in President Donald Trump’s administration have repeatedly hinted at the existence of an inquiry targeting Omar, a Somali-born Democrat whose status as an immigrant to the U.S. and left-wing views have repeatedly drawn criticism from Republicans and senior Trump officials.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said last month that there was an “ongoing investigation” related in part to whether Omar lied on her immigration forms and that “something’s going to happen.”
Omar responded to the search with a statement on X that called it an “attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement.”
“For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation,” she said. “I will not be silenced.”
Though the Republican focus on Omar’s background dates back years, the search of her home took place three weeks before the November midterms, in which Omar is on the ballot for reelection. The Justice Department has historically sought to avoid public investigative actions involving a candidate within 60 days of a primary or general election.
“For years, Donald Trump and far-right extremists have relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Omar with vile personal attacks and baseless accusations,” top House Democratic leaders said in a statement. “Now, less than 30 days until the midterm election, his violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family.
Trump has frequently targeted Omar
Trump as recently as this past weekend brought up Omar at a rally in Tennessee, where he attacked her upbringing and suggested that Vice President JD Vance “and our people” were investigating her.
Vance has in the past accused Omar of committing immigration fraud — an allegation she has denied — and has said he and a top White House official were trying to figure out how to investigate her.
A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security, of which Homeland Security Investigations is part, referred questions about the search to the Justice Department. The Justice Department said in a statement that Monday’s enforcement action “is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation.”
The street was blocked off Monday morning as HSI agents remained near the home.
Omar has long been a target for Republicans
Omar, who was first elected to the House in 2018, represents Minnesota’s 5th District, including Minneapolis. She is part of The Squad of progressive lawmakers who are a vibrant political force on the left wing of Congress but have also endured repeated attacks from Trump, dating back to his first term. She was one of the first two Muslim-American women in the House and the first African refugee to be elected to Congress.
When Republicans swept control of the House in 2023, they voted to oust Omar from the House Foreign Affairs Committee, citing her anti-Israel remarks.
In January, Trump lashed out at Omar during a rally in Iowa hours before an assailant sprayed the congresswoman during her own town hall meeting in Minneapolis with a substance that turned out to be vinegar. The attacker was sentenced recently to 14 months in prison.
Republicans have raised questions about Omar’s past since before she was even elected, including asserting that she had married her brother and committed immigration fraud. Omar has broadly denied the allegations as “disgusting lies.”
“It certainly seems like something fishy is there, but everybody’s entitled to equal justice under the laws,” Vance told reporters in May. “So we’re going to investigate it. We’re going to take a look at it. If we think there’s a crime, we’re going to prosecute that crime.”
In a separate interview with conservative podcaster Benny Johnson, Vance said without offering evidence that “we actually think that Ilhan Omar definitely committed immigration fraud against the United States of America.”
He said that he and deputy White House chief of staff Stephen Miller had been discussing it and “trying to look at what the remedies are.”
“That’s the thing that we’re trying to figure out,” he said. “What are the legal remedies now that we know that she’s committed immigration fraud. How do you go after her? How do you investigate her? How do you actually do the thing? How do you build the case necessary to get some, some, some justice for the American people?”
Omar’s office has defended her against past allegations
Omar’s office in March dismissed Vance’s claims as fabricated and defamatory.
“This is rich coming from someone who literally said they were willing to ‘create stories’ to redirect the media,” Omar’s chief of staff, Connor McNutt, said in a statement.
“This is a ridiculous lie and desperate attempt to distract from the pedophile protection party’s unpopular war of choice, increasing gas prices, and rapidly dropping polling numbers,” McNutt said at the time of the vice president’s allegations and comments.
___
Associated Press writers Lisa Mascaro, Michelle L. Price and River Zhang in Washington, Kathy McCormack in Concord, N.H., Mike Catalini in Morrisville, Pa., and Meg Kinnard in Columbia, S.C., contributed.

sources.news_title: Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar's home as part of a criminal investigation, sources say
sources.text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Federal agents have searched Democratic U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home as part of a criminal investigation, according to people familiar with the matter.
The people say the search was conducted by Homeland Security Investigations agents. The people were not authorized to publicly discuss an ongoing investigation and spoke on the condition of anonymity.
Details about the investigation are unclear. The Justice Department said in a statement Monday that HSI agents executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the department in the Washington, D.C., area but provided no other details.
An email seeking comment has been sent to a representative for Omar.
JD Vance has accused Rep. Omar of immigration fraud, without offering evidence
Details about what Homeland Security agents were looking for in their search of the Minnesota Democrat’s home early Monday have not been announced, and Omar has yet to comment.
In the past, the vice president has accused her of committing immigration fraud, without providing details, and has said that he and deputy White House chief of staff Stephen Miller were trying to figure out how to investigate the congresswoman.
Omar has broadly denied the allegations as “disgusting lies.” Her office in March dismissed Vance’s claims as fabricated and defamatory.
“This is rich coming from someone who literally said they were willing to ‘create stories’ to redirect the media,” Omar’s chief of staff, Connor McNutt, said in a statement.
House Democratic leaders condemn the search of Ilhan Omar’s home as an ‘abuse of power’ by the Trump administration
“For years, Donald Trump and far-right extremists have relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Omar with vile personal attacks and baseless accusations,” House Democratic leaders said in a statement. “Now, less than 30 days until the midterm election, his violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family.”
The search of the Minnesota congresswoman‘s home so close to next month’s midterm contests that will determine control of the House and Senate was swiftly condemned by top Democrats in Congress and raised questions about the timing given longstanding Justice Department protocol to avoid overt investigative steps involving political candidates in the direct run-up to an election.
Omar calls search the ‘latest escalation’ in Trump’s ‘intimidation’ campaign
“For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns,” she said. “This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced.”
Omar’s spokesperson calls raid ‘outrageous’ and ‘unprecedented’
“This raid by Trump’s DHS is an outrageous abuse of power and an unprecedented escalation in the weaponization of federal law enforcement to target political enemies,” Jacklyn Rogers, Omar’s spokesperson, said in a statement.
“For a decade, Donald Trump has relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Ilhan Omar with inflammatory rhetoric, repeatedly putting a target on her back. Now, those attacks have escalated to a pointless federal raid. The Congresswoman has done nothing wrong. No president should be able to use the power of the federal government to intimidate his political enemies.”
Fellow members of The Squad express support for Omar
Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York called the search of Omar’s home “an unprecedented abuse of power,” saying Trump’s administration had long “launched slanderous attacks” against the Minnesota Democrat.
Michigan Rep. Rashida Tlaib said the search is “exactly what a fascist police state does.”
Omar, Tlaib and Ocasio-Cortez are part of The Squad, a group of progressive lawmakers who are a vibrant political force on the left wing of Congress and have endured repeated attacks from Trump, dating back to his first term.
Both Tlaib and Ocasio-Cortez off on their social media posts by saying, “I stand with Ilhan.”
Democrats condemn Omar raid as political targeting ahead of election
Across social media, congressional Democrats criticized Trump for the search of Omar’s home.
Calling it “unprecedented, but unfortunately not surprising,” Michigan Rep. Debbie Dingell wrote that Trump had “repeatedly targeted Congresswoman Omar with hateful rhetoric, contributing to death threats and violence.”
Arizona Rep. Adellita Grijalva said it represented “the latest — and darkest — chapter of Trump’s racist political persecution against Ilhan Omar and the entire Somali-American community.”
Saying Trump was “weaponizing our government against his perceived political opponents,” Colorado Rep. Jason Crow referenced the administration’s unsuccessful attempt to indict him and other congressional Democrats for a video calling on service members to defy “illegal orders.”
Associated Press writers Kathy McCormack in Concord, N.H., and Mike Catalini in Morrisville, Pa., contributed.

sources.news_title: Rep. Ilhan Omar's Home Raided By Federal Agents
sources.text:
WASHINGTON ― Homeland Security Investigations agents raided the home of Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) on Monday morning as part of a criminal investigation into the Minnesota progressive who has long been the target of ugly attacks by President Donald Trump.
“Today in the Washington, D.C, area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice,” a Justice Department spokesperson told HuffPost in a statement. “This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation.”
The DOJ spokesperson would not give any details about the justification for its probe, which is reportedly related to immigration paperwork filled out by Omar’s now-deceased father when she was a child. Omar, who is Somali-American, came to the United States as a refugee in 1995, and has been a U.S. citizen for 26 years.
The Department of Homeland Security and the White House both deferred to the DOJ for any comment.
The Minnesota Democrat, one of the first Muslim women elected to Congress and an outspoken critic of Trump’s policies, has endured years of racist and Islamophobic attacks by the president. In a statement, she ripped Trump for once again trying to politically intimidate her, this time weeks out from the midterm elections.
“I’m ok,” Omar said on social media. “Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement. For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation.”
She added: “I will not be silenced.”
Separately, Omar’s spokeswoman Jackie Rogers called the Trump administration’s raid “an outrageous abuse of power.”
“Donald Trump has relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Ilhan Omar with inflammatory rhetoric, repeatedly putting a target on her back,” Rogers told HuffPost in a statement. “Now, those attacks have escalated to a pointless federal raid. The Congresswoman has done nothing wrong. No president should be able to use the power of the federal government to intimidate his political enemies.”
The decision to conduct a raid within the 60-day window before the November elections appears to break with standard DOJ practice of avoiding such investigative steps involving political candidates this close to an election.
On top of that, if there is any merit to the administration’s investigation ― which has yet to be shown ― immigrants who obtain citizenship status through fraud that they didn’t know about can avoid consequences for it, like losing a green card, says Aaron Reichlin-Melnick of the American Immigration Council.
“So this is *even weaker* than it already seems,” he said on social media of the Trump administration’s apparent justification for its raid on Omar’s home.
Tom Homan, Trump’s border czar, declined to offer any details on the raid during a Monday appearance on Fox News.
“The specifics of the investigation, I think I need to turn that over to Todd Blanche or Markwayne Mullin,” he said. “I don’t want to get ahead of them.”
Homan has previously said the administration was investigating Omar over allegations — made by the president without evidence — that she married her brother to get U.S. citizenship.
At the time, Omar reacted to the news, saying the probe was launched “because they are sick.”

sources.news_title: Feds Raid Home of Trump Nemesis He Wants Thrown in Jail
sources.text:
Feds Raid Home of Trump Nemesis He Wants Thrown in Jail
The president has long railed against Somali-born Minnesota Rep. Ilhan Omar.
Federal officials carried out a dawn raid at the home of a Democratic congresswoman who’s long been a thorn in Donald Trump’s side.
The Homeland Security Investigations agency (HSI) searched 44-year-old Rep. Ilhan Omar’s D.C.-area residence on Monday morning, sources familiar with the operation told Fox News.
“Today in the Washington, D.C., area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice,” a DOJ spokesperson told the Daily Beast. “This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation.”
They said that the raid forms part of a criminal probe into her immigration paperwork, which her late father filled out after the family emigrated to the U.S. from Somalia when she was a child.
Trump, 80, has long railed against the progressive Minnesota congresswoman. “‘Scammer’ Ilhan Omar and her absolutely terrible friends from Somalia should all be in jail right now, or far worse, send them back to Somalia,” he wrote in a Truth Social post in January.
The president’s border czar, Tom Homan, announced last month that the Department of Homeland Security was conducting a criminal investigation into Omar, who has been a U.S. citizen since 2000.
The congresswoman told Fox News on September 18 that federal investigators had not contacted her about the probe. She dismissed the allegations surrounding her immigration history as a politically motivated attack, telling the network: “The right wing has always had this s--- going, so I don’t really worry about it.”

Omar has become a favorite target of Trump and his allies amid a vast welfare fraud scandal in Minnesota, where prosecutors have brought cases against dozens of defendants, many of them of Somali descent.
The president has repeatedly attacked the state’s Somali community, and Omar in particular, over the theft of public money, despite no evidence connecting the congresswoman to any of those schemes.
His administration cited the scandal as justification for its aggressive immigration crackdown that saw thousands of federal agents descend on Minnesota late last year.
The operation prompted outrage across the country after officers shot and killed two American citizens, Renee Good and Alex Pretti, during separate confrontations in Minneapolis in January.
Other officials have thrown their weight behind Trump’s attacks on Omar. Vice President JD Vance said earlier this year that the DOJ was looking at whether Omar had engaged in immigration fraud, while Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has suggested deporting her if authorities can establish wrongdoing involving her family’s arrival in America.
Omar escaped Somalia’s civil war with her family when she was eight. She spent four years living in a Kenyan refugee camp before securing refugee status in America in 1995. She became a citizen five years later, at 17, and made history when she was elected in 2018 as the first Somali American to enter Congress.
Her bitter feud with Trump stretches back to his first presidency. During a 2019 campaign rally in North Carolina, his supporters erupted into chants of “send her back” as he attacked the Minnesota Democrat.
The president renewed his calls to expel Omar in February after she interrupted his State of the Union address to protest his immigration crackdown. He declared that she and fellow Democratic Rep. Rashida Tlaib, who is of Palestinian descent, should be sent “back from where they came—as fast as possible.”
Tlaib, like Omar, is an American citizen—Tlaib was born in Michigan.
Trump, who has previously called Somali Americans “garbage,” renewed his attacks with a vitriolic Truth Social post last week. “The once Great State of Minnesota is being taken over by Somali Immigrants,” he wrote. “There is Violence, Murder, and Mayhem all over the State. The people of Minnesota must fight back.”
The Daily Beast has contacted Omar’s office for comment. The Department of Homeland Security declined to comment.
The White House declined to comment.
