sources.news_title: Ilhan Omar Responds as Home Searched By Homeland Security Amid Probe
sources.text:
Representative Ilhan Omar denounced a federal raid Monday as politically motivated hours after agents searched her Washington home.
"Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement," Omar wrote on X. "For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced."
Jacklyn Rogers, Omar’s communications director, characterized the raid as an “outrageous" abuse of power.
“For a decade, Donald Trump has relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Ilhan Omar with inflammatory rhetoric, repeatedly putting a target on her back,” Rogers told Newsweek in a statement. “Now, those attacks have escalated to a pointless federal raid. The Congresswoman has done nothing wrong. No president should be able to use the power of the federal government to intimidate his political enemies.”
President Trump acknowledged the raid late Monday when asked if he had known about the operation in advance.
"Well, I understand they’re looking at her very carefully," Trump told reporters. "I've always found her to be totally crooked personally, but that has nothing to do with me. I think she's a terrible person. She’s just a complainer — she comes from a country that is a non-country."
Homeland Security agents searched Omar’s Washington, D.C., home earlier Monday, marking a significant escalation in federal scrutiny of the Minnesota Democrat just over three weeks before Election Day. The department confirmed that the search was part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation but did not publicly provide a detailed account of the evidence or identify all potential targets.
“Today in the Washington, D.C., area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice,” a Department of Justice (DOJ) spokesperson told Newsweek. “This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation.”
The warrant lists several potential immigration offenses under investigation, including false statements and fraud in immigration paperwork, as well as a general conspiracy charge, The New York Times reported, citing a person familiar with the document. Newsweek has not independently reviewed the warrant.
In response to Newsweek’s request for comment, the Department of Homeland Security said: “We refer you to the Department of Justice.”
In a video obtained by Fox News, an unidentified person asks an HSI officer outside Omar's residence whether the operation was “an illegal immigration raid.” The officer replied, “No, it’s not,” but described the scene only as “police activity.” Asked directly whether agents were raiding the congresswoman's home, the officer said, “I’m not going to discuss anything with you.”
Why Is Ilhan Omar’s Home Being Searched?
The search warrant reportedly identifies several possible immigration offenses under investigation, but it remains unclear precisely what conduct federal authorities are examining or whether Omar herself is suspected of committing a crime. The search, however, follows months of federal scrutiny concerning Omar's immigration history.
Last month, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said authorities were examining Omar’s immigration history, including the long-running allegation that she married her brother to help him enter the U.S. Omar has repeatedly denied the allegation, which has not been substantiated.
"There may be more to this, the whole family migration and possibly some illegal activity for them to come to the United States to begin with,” Mullin said.
Earlier this year, Vice President JD Vance said that the DOJ was investigating Omar, again over alleged immigration fraud. The comments came as fraud in Minnesota became a national topic, and after Omar had been faced with accusations of involvement in the “Feeding Our Future” scandal, in which a nonprofit secured $250 million in federal reimbursements by lying about pandemic-era activities.
“Any claim that I had knowledge of this scheme is flat-out false," Omar said in a statement shared with Newsweek at the time. “As I stated from the beginning, stealing millions of dollars under the guise of feeding hungry children to bankroll lavish lifestyles and extravagant expenses is reprehensible."
Her finances and those of her husband have also come under scrutiny in recent years. In mid-2025, Omar filed an annual financial disclosure form that put her family assets at between $6 million and $30 million, a surge from the previous year that would have placed her among the wealthiest Democrats in the House.
Following scrutiny, however, Omar revised the filing, which is common among members of Congress, significantly downgrading the value of her assets. Her representatives said that this was due to "incomplete information" originally being provided by the accountants of her husband, Tim Mynett.
“The accounting error created a misleading picture of far greater wealth," Jacklyn Rogers, a spokesperson for Omar, told Newsweek in April. "The congresswoman amended her disclosures voluntarily as soon as the discrepancy was identified. The amended disclosure is now complete and accurate.”
The Office of Congressional Conduct investigated the discrepancy but last month dismissed any misconduct allegations, Omar's office said.
Reaction to the Search
Democratic National Committee Chair Ken Martin described the search as politically motivated and defended Omar.
“A new low for the Trump administration: raiding the home of a U.S. congresswoman weeks out from Election Day,” Martin wrote on X.
“This is the latest in a series of bigoted and unfounded attacks against my friend,” he added. “Ilhan is a fighter who will not back down. I am proud to stand with her.”
Republican Representative Nancy Mace, meanwhile, suggested without evidence that the search concerned allegations about Omar’s immigration history, citing records she tried to subpoena in Congress and repeating the unsubstantiated allegation that Omar married her brother.
“This morning HSI raided her home with a judicially authorized warrant, presumably over the same paperwork,” she added. “If the fraud is proven, she should be denaturalized and deported home to Somalia.”
Democratic strategist Mike Nellis said the timing of the search represented a break with established practice and accused the administration of using the investigation to target Omar.
“DHS typically avoids operations like this so close to an election,” Nellis wrote on X. “That’s another norm shattered, and Republicans will regret tearing it up someday.”
“They know the immigration stuff with Omar is bulls***,” he added. “This raid was part harassment, part fishing expedition to dig up something embarrassing.”
The Council on American-Islamic Relations also condemned Monday’s raid as a “obvious act” of political persecution.
“President Trump has spent years obsessively smearing Rep. Omar and demanding that law enforcement target her,” CAIR national executive director Nihad Awad told Newsweek in a statement. “So have other anti-Muslim extremists who cannot stand the sight of an accomplished Black woman wearing a hijab and speaking up for human rights while serving her constituents in the halls of Congress. Today’s raid is undoubtedly a result of those demands.”
Who Is Ilhan Omar?
Omar, 44, has represented Minnesota’s 5th Congressional District since 2019, having secured 78 percent of the vote over Republican candidate Jennifer Zielinski in 2018. Prior to that, Omar served in the Minnesota House of Representatives.
She currently serves on several House committees, including the House Budget Committee and the Committee on Education and the Workforce.
Since entering Congress, Omar has cultivated a reputation as one of the most outspoken progressives in her party, and is a member of “The Squad”—an unofficial group of four female Democratic lawmakers elected in 2018: Omar, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York, Ayanna Pressley of Massachusetts and Rashida Tlaib of Michigan.
Omar was born in Somalia but fled the country at age 8, later becoming the first Somali American elected to Congress. However, her heritage and journey to national prominence have made her a target of Republican attacks during her political career, including from President Donald Trump.
Trump was criticized during his first term for saying that Democratic congresswomen should “go back and help fix the totally broken and crime-infested places from which they came.”
In November 2025, Trump posted to Truth Social that Omar should “go back!” in response to a video of her speaking at an event in Somalia.
In January, Trump wrote that she "should be in jail, or even a worse punishment, sent back to Somalia.” Omar responded on X, writing: "Sorry, Trump, your support is collapsing and you’re panicking. Right on cue, you’re deflecting from your failures with lies and conspiracy theories about me. Years of ‘investigations’ have found nothing.”
Can Ilhan Omar Be Deported?
As a naturalized U.S. citizen, Omar cannot be deported unless her citizenship is revoked through a formal court process proving that it was obtained fraudulently.
During a podcast interview in March, Vance said that the Trump administration believes Omar "definitely committed immigration fraud against the United States of America.”
However, no criminal charges have been filed and no denaturalization proceedings relating to immigration fraud have yet been publicly disclosed.
Ilhan Omar Reelection, What the Polls Show
Omar is seeking another term in the House in November, having won her primary in August with more than 80 percent of the vote. She is favored to win against Republican John Nagel, a former state trooper.
The polling aggregator Decision Desk HQ currently puts her win probability at 99 percent with a projected margin of +64. All other major forecasters list Minnesota’s 5th Congressional District as a safe seat for Democrats.
Update, 11:48 a.m. ET: This article was updated with additional information.
Contact Newsweek editors on this story: Daniel Orton and Geoffrey Rowland.

sources.news_title: Federal agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home as part of criminal investigation, AP sources say
Omar says she won’t ‘be silenced’ by search of her home and blasts Trump’s ‘intimidation’ campaign
sources.text:
By ALANNA DURKIN RICHER and ERIC TUCKER
WASHINGTON (AP) — Federal agents on Monday searched the home of Democratic U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar, a startling escalation in a criminal investigation that brings renewed focus to the frequent target of Trump administration derision in the final weeks of her reelection bid.
The search of the Minnesota congresswoman’s home so close to next month’s midterm contests that will determine control of the House and the Senate was swiftly condemned by top Democrats in Congress, who raised questions about the timing given longstanding Justice Department protocol to avoid overt investigative steps involving political candidates in the direct run-up to an election. Omar, an outspoken critic of President Donald Trump, said she was being targeted as one of the Republican’s “political enemies.”
The scope of the investigation was unclear, though Trump and officials in his administration have repeatedly referred in recent months to the existence of an inquiry into Omar, a Somali-born Democrat whose status as an immigrant to the U.S. and left-wing views have drawn scrutiny from the White House and other Republicans.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin last month cited an “ongoing investigation” that he suggested was examining potential fraud in her family’s immigration paperwork. “Something’s going to happen,” he said in a potential foreshadowing of the search.
In a statement on X on Monday, Omar called the search an “attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement.”
“For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation,” she said. “I will not be silenced.”
At a political rally in Ohio later Monday, Trump attacked Omar’s Somali origins, saying, “She’s telling us about the Constitution, and she comes from one of the worst countries anywhere on the planet.” The crowd responded by shouting, “Deport.”
Though the Republican focus on Omar’s background dates back years, the search notably took place three weeks before the November midterms, in which Omar is seeking reelection. The Justice Department has historically sought to avoid public investigative actions involving a candidate within 60 days of a primary or general election. Top Democrats seized on the timing as the latest instance in what they said was the “continued corrupt weaponization” against Trump’s perceived adversaries.
“For years, Donald Trump and far-right extremists have relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Omar with vile personal attacks and baseless accusations,” said a joint statement from House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and other top congressional Democrats. “Now, less than 30 days until the midterm election, his violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family.”
Trump says he had “nothing to do” with search
The search was carried out by agents with Homeland Security Investigations, which is part of the Department of Homeland Security.
A DHS spokesperson referred questions to the Justice Department, which said in a statement that HSI agents had executed a judicially authorized search warrant in the Washington, D.C., area related to an ongoing federal criminal investigation but provided no other details.
The street around Omar’s home was blocked off Monday morning as some HSI agents removed boxes labeled “Seized Property Evidence.”
The operation came just days after Trump referred pejoratively to Omar at a rally in Tennessee as coming from a country of “crime and squalor” and suggested that Vice President JD Vance “and our people” were investigating her. Hours after the search, Trump told reporters he had “nothing to do” with it and it’s “really up to the DOJ.”
Trump suggested he didn’t know what was happening with the investigation even as he seemed to suggest that Omar was engaged in suspect behavior.
Vance has in the past accused Omar of committing immigration fraud, an allegation she has denied, and has said the administration was looking for pathways to investigate her.
Omar has long been a target for Republicans
Omar, who was first elected to the House in 2018, represents Minnesota’s 5th District, including Minneapolis. She is part of The Squad of progressive lawmakers who are a vibrant political force on the left wing of Congress but have also endured repeated attacks from Trump, dating back to his first term. She was one of the first two Muslim-American women in the House and the first African refugee to be elected to Congress.
When Republicans swept control of the House in 2023, they voted to oust Omar from the House Foreign Affairs Committee, citing her anti-Israel remarks.
In January, Trump lashed out at Omar during a rally in Iowa hours before an assailant sprayed the congresswoman during her own town hall meeting in Minneapolis with a substance that turned out to be vinegar. The attacker was sentenced to 14 months in prison.
Omar has repeatedly refuted allegations about her marriage and immigration status raised by conservative critics, even before she joined Congress.
According to her House biography, Omar has said she and her family fled Somalia’s civil war when she was 8: “The family spent four years in a refugee camp in Kenya before coming to the United States in 1990s. In 1997, she moved to Minneapolis with her family.”
Conservative online sites have alleged that Omar married a brother to commit immigration fraud. Omar has broadly denied the allegations as “disgusting lies” and called the insinuation “absurd and offensive.”
“It certainly seems like something fishy is there, but everybody’s entitled to equal justice under the laws,” Vance told reporters in May. “So we’re going to investigate it. We’re going to take a look at it. If we think there’s a crime, we’re going to prosecute that crime. And that’s something the Department of Justice is looking at right now.”
In an interview last March with conservative podcaster Benny Johnson, Vance said without offering evidence that “we actually think that Ilhan Omar definitely committed immigration fraud against the United States of America.” Omar’s office at the time dismissed Vance’s claims as fabricated and defamatory.
Last month, when the podcaster Johnson reminded Mullin about Vance’s comments on Omar and asked whether anything would happen from that investigation, the Homeland Security secretary responded, “Something’s going to happen.”
He cited an “ongoing investigation” that he suggested was examining potential fraud in the family’s immigration paperwork.
“If we actually move a case forward, it’s not a political case. It’s actually a case because they did things wrong,” Mullin said. “If you decided to break the law or lie on the information that you gave to the United States, to be able to come into the United States … there’s no expiration to that.”
Associated Press writers Lisa Mascaro, Michelle L. Price and River Zhang in Washington, Kathy McCormack in Concord, N.H., Mike Catalini in Morrisville, Pa., and Meg Kinnard in Columbia, S.C., contributed.

The investigation had previously been acknowledged by White House border czar Tom Homan, who revealed in September that federal authorities were examining allegations involving Omar. Homan described the matter as a criminal investigation but declined to discuss the specific evidence or potential violations under review.
At the time, Homan emphasized that elected officials are subject to the same immigration laws as other Americans. He indicated that investigators would examine credible allegations of immigration violations or marriage fraud regardless of the individual’s political position.
Omar, who was born in Somalia, came to the United States as a refugee with her family during childhood. She later became a naturalized American citizen and was elected to Congress in 2018, becoming one of the first Muslim women to serve in the House of Representatives.
Her immigration history has faced scrutiny for years, particularly regarding allegations involving her previous marriage to Ahmed Nur Said Elmi in 2009. Political opponents have alleged that the marriage was connected to immigration fraud, including an unproven claim that Elmi was her brother.

Federal authorities have not publicly established whether the current investigation concerns those longstanding marriage allegations, her childhood immigration records or additional matters. The available information specifically identifies paperwork completed by her father as an area under examination.
The search of Omar’s residence follows earlier reporting that federal immigration authorities had declined to release certain records involving the congresswoman under the Freedom of Information Act. The latest investigation raises questions about how federal authorities will handle allegations involving a sitting member of Congress. Investigators must follow established legal procedures, including obtaining judicial authorization when required to search private property.

Rep. Ilhan Omar’s DC home raided by DHS as part of probe into Dem’s immigration paperwork
See more of our coverage in your search results.
WASHINGTON — Minnesota Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home was raided early Monday morning by the Department of Homeland Security as part of an ongoing criminal fraud investigation into the Somalia-born congresswoman’s immigration paperwork.
Agents wearing Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) jackets arrived outside Omar’s Washington, DC, home to execute a search warrant and were later observed removing belongings early Monday on the quiet residential street.
The Post saw agents carrying boxes out of the residence to government vehicles, one of which was white and marked with a pink “X,” as the congresswoman’s neighbors looked on in disbelief.
The more-than-half-a-million-dollar bungalow appears to have gotten a significant facelift since it was sold in 2018 and now sports a bright door on a street where Omar’s neighbors sport “Free Palestine” and other like-minded signage.
The raid was the result of a years-long criminal investigation involving whistleblowers and related to alleged false statements made on Omar’s immigration papers, according to sources familiar with the case.
“Today in the Washington, D.C. area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice,” a DOJ spokesperson said, noting the action was part of “an ongoing federal investigation.”
Federal agents presented evidence to a DC court to obtain the search warrant for the sitting congresswoman’s home, which a judge signed off on, border czar Tom Homan said later on Fox News Monday.
“I’m ok. Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement,” Omar said in a statement on X later. “For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation.”
“I will not be silenced,” the congresswoman vowed.
Trump insisted he had “nothing” to do with ordering the raid.
“I think she’s a terrible person, but that’s really up to the DOJ. I have nothing to do with it,” Trump told reporters later, saying that he understood investigators had been “looking at her very carefully.”
“I’ve always found her to be totally crooked personally, but that has nothing to do with me,” the president added. “I think she’s a terrible person. Just a complainer. She comes from a country that is a non-country. And then she comes over here and she complains about our Constitution.”
Neighbors said Omar, 44, and her family had lived there for at least the past three years.
One described hearing “loud banging” on the representative’s door at around 4 or 5 a.m., followed by “a man screaming, ‘Open the door, open the door.”
The unidentified neighbor said they didn’t know if Omar was at home at the time of the raid, and that agents had been going in and out of the property all morning.
They were “very good neighbors,” one resident told The Post, describing as “totally ridiculous” the early-morning raid.
A source told The Post that authorities are “investigating [Omar’s] immigration history, which includes her family’s history, as part of the probe.”
Officials are expected to attempt to revoke her US citizenship if evidence shows it was obtained through concealment of a material fact or willful misrepresentation.
Authorities are looking into whether Omar used a different name in Somalia, and whether her family immigrated legally, which could impact her own status inside the US.
It comes just weeks after Border Czar Tom Homan revealed that Omar was under an ongoing “criminal” investigation.
Omar has long been dogged by allegations that she married her brother in order to help him secure a US visa or student loans — though sources indicated that Monday’s raid didn’t appear to be tied to those accusations.
Omar and Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, a British citizen, were married in 2009. They divorced in 2017.
The progressive Democrat has also been accused of entering the US in 1995 under a false name or secondary family identity to bypass refugee processing backlogs.
Meanwhile, the controversial lawmaker has faced questions about alleged tax discrepancies, after a 2019 Minnesota state campaign finance board found that she filed joint tax returns with Ahmed Hirsi, the father of her children, in 2014 and 2015 — while she was still legally married to her first husband.
Omar has consistently denied that Elmi is her brother, branding the claims as baseless bigotry.
She said she entered into a religious marriage with Hirsi in 2002, but they later separated and she legally married Elmi in 2009.
The congresswoman said she and Elmi separated two years later, in 2011, before she reconciled with Hirsi.
She and Hirsi were legally divorced in October 2019, around two years after her divorce from Elmi in 2017.
In March 2020, Omar announced that she had married Tim Mynett, a political consultant who had done work for her campaign.
Mynett’s subsequent venture capital and wine businesses ended up inflating the couple’s net worth by tens of millions of dollars in recent years — though Omar has since blamed accounting errors for the discrepancy.
The search on Omar’s residence more likely came as a result of inconsistencies or inaccurate statements that Omar’s father, Nur Omar Mohamed, may have made for his daughter when applying for citizenship, sources say.
Mohamed served as an officer in the Somali National Army before dictator Mohamed Siad Barre was toppled, prompting him to depart with his family for the US.
The future congresswoman is the youngest of seven children Mohamed and his wife had while in Mogadishu, Somalia, before they were granted asylum and emigrated to Arlington, Va., in 1995.
Two years later, the family moved to Minneapolis where Omar would attend high school. She eventually became a US citizen at age 17 in 2000.
The Minnesota Democrat’s dad died of complications due to COVID-19 at the age of 67 in June 2020. Mohamed worked in the state as a postal employee and cab driver, as his daughter’s star rose in state and later federal politics.
In May, Vice President JD Vance announced that the DOJ, alongside federal immigration authorities, was reviewing potential instances of immigration fraud and family financial disclosures.
This followed an April amendment to Omar’s federal financial disclosures that adjusted reported asset values.
The HSI is the main investigative arm of Homeland Security, with a scope that includes investigating cross-border crime and global threats, including human trafficking, child sexual exploitation, drug smuggling, and cybercrime.
No formal criminal charges or court filings have been brought against Omar to date, while her legal counsel and spokespeople maintain that her naturalization process and financial disclosures fully comply with federal law.
After the raid, Omar’s spokesperson and other Democrats accused the Trump administration of weaponizing the federal government to target the president’s political enemies.
“For a decade, Donald Trump has relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Ilhan Omar with inflammatory rhetoric, repeatedly putting a target on her back,” spokesperson Jacklyn Rogers said in a statement. “The congresswoman has done nothing wrong.”
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) in a statement said Trump’s “violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family.”
“DHS raiding a member of congress’s home is exactly what a fascist police state does,” added fellow “Squad” Rep. Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.) in an X post.

sources.news_title: US Federal Agents Search Ilhan Omar’s Washington-Area Residence in Ongoing Criminal Investigation
US federal agents search Ilhan Omar's home
sources.text:
US federal agents search Ilhan Omar's home
Digital Desk |
Washington, Oct 12 (IANS) Federal agents searched the Washington-area residence of Democratic Congresswoman Ilhan Omar on Monday as part of an ongoing criminal investigation, escalating federal scrutiny of one of President Donald Trump's most outspoken political opponents.
The US Department of Justice confirmed that agents from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the investigative arm of the Department of Homeland Security, executed a court-authorised search warrant in the Washington area.
"Today in the Washington, D.C. area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice," a Justice Department spokesperson said.
"This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation," the spokesperson added.
The department did not identify the suspected offences, disclose what investigators were seeking or say whether any evidence had been seized.
Fox News, citing sources familiar with the investigation, reported that the inquiry concerned immigration documents prepared by Omar's late father when she was a child.
The reported focus of the investigation could not be independently confirmed from the Justice Department's statement.
Omar, a Somali-born naturalised American citizen who represents Minnesota's Fifth Congressional District, has repeatedly rejected allegations questioning the legitimacy of her immigration history.
No criminal charges against the congresswoman had been announced in connection with Monday's search.
The development comes amid a prolonged confrontation between Omar and Trump, who has repeatedly questioned her background and criticised her political positions.
In January this year, President Donald Trump publicly referred to an investigation involving Omar and made allegations about her personal finances.
The latest search marks a significant development because federal investigators obtained judicial authorisation to enter a residence associated with a sitting member of Congress.
A search warrant requires judicial approval based on probable cause. Its execution does not establish that the subject of an investigation has committed an offence.
The investigation also comes just three weeks before the November 3 congressional midterm elections, when control of the House of Representatives and Senate will be contested.
Omar is seeking re-election in Minnesota, where immigration enforcement has emerged as a politically contentious issue.
The congresswoman has been particularly critical of the Trump administration's immigration policies, including enforcement operations affecting immigrant communities in Minnesota.
The administration, meanwhile, has argued for stronger immigration enforcement and closer scrutiny of suspected fraud involving immigration documents and citizenship applications.
Omar, 44, was born in Somalia and arrived in the United States as a refugee during the 1990s. She became a US citizen and was first elected to Congress in 2018, becoming one of the first two Muslim women elected to the House of Representatives.
She has been a prominent critic of Trump's domestic and foreign policies. Her political career has frequently placed her at the centre of national debates over immigration, race, religion and the treatment of minority communities in the United States.
